details.body: O, Oh, interj. he, BoH, ayi, aye, are; hA, ahaha (sorrow). 2 aho (joy and surprise), haMta, aho, bata. 3 AH (anger &c.). 4 A, AM; ‘oh for’ ex. by api nAma; ‘oh for a lodge in a wilderness’ api nAma vipine nivAsaM laBeya; ‘oh that’ See Would.

O, OH: I In addressing:(1) he;(2) Bo BoH, or Bo Bo (gen. to men), o, courtiers: Bo Bo kulacAriRaH, Vi.;(3) ayi or aye (expr. of tenderness), o, you unbearing: ayi asahane, Ra.; (4) re or are (to inferiors or in contempt), o, you fool: are mUrKa, Mr.;(5) hA (in sorrow), o, my father, o, my mothers, o, my dear friend Sugriva: hA tAta, hA mAtaraH, hA priyasaKa sugrIva, U; (6) by voc.II Of joy and surprise:(1) aho, oh, how grand and beautiful is earth: aho udAraramaRIyA pfTivI, Sa.;(2) ayi or aye, oh, you also don't know: ayi tvamapi na vetsi, Mah. III Of surprise, anger, contempt: AH, oh, I understand, very well: AH jYAtaM, tizWa, Mu. IV Of grief: hA: v. Alas.
O! exclam. (Vocative) BoH, Bos, Bo, BoBo, he. — (To inferiors) re, are, arere, hE, aho. — (Expressive of surprise, grief, an- ger, &c.) A, AH, hA, ahaha, ahahA, hanta, aho, ahovat.
OAF , s. sTUlabudDiH m., sTUlajanaH, mandabudDiH, jaqabudDiH, mUrKaH, mUQaH, barbaraH.
OAFISH , a. sTUlasvaBAvaH -vA -vaM, mandasvaBAvaH &c., abudDiH -dDiH -dDi.
Oak, s. siMdUraH.
OAK: a tree: sindUraH, Williams.
OAK , s. sindUraH, sindUravfkzaH, vanavfkzaBedaH, vanyapAdapaBedaH, vanarAjiH.
OAKEN: (1) sindUra- in comp. (?);(2) sindUra- kAzWamayaH (yI, yaM) (?).
OAKEN , s. sindUrakAzWamayaH -yI -yaM, sindUravfkzanirmmitaH -tA -taM.
Oakum, s. KaMqitarajju f.
OAKUM: perh. talapatram (comp. Bengali kAlApAti).
OAKUM , s. jIrRarajjuKaRqaH, SaRaKaRqaH, KaRqitarajjuH m. f., SaRasUtrakaM.
Oar, s. kze(kzi)paRi-RI f., nO-nOkA-daMqaH. v. t. kzepaRyA cal c. or vah c.; See Row. Oarsman, s. nOdaMqaDaraH.
OAR: (1) daRqaH (when the sense is clear); (2) kzepaRiH, -RI.
OAR (v.): v. To row. O.ed: by comp., four-o.: caturdaRqa (f. RqA).
OAR , s. kzepaRiH -RI f., kzipaRiH -RI, kzapaRI, nOkAdaRqaH, nOdaRqaH, aritraM, AritraM, taraRqaH, tariraTaH.
OARASMAN , s. nOkAdaRqaDaraH -DArI m. (n), nOdaRqacAlakaH.
OARED , a. daRqavAn -vatI -vat (t), daRqI -RqinI -Rqi (n); ‘four- oared,’ caturdaRqavAn &c., caturdaRqI &c.
Oasis, s. (marumaDye) SAdvalasTalaM, ramyasTAnaM.
OASIS , s. maruBUmimaDyagataM SAqvalasTalaM, marumaDyasTaM SAdvalasTAnaM.
OAT, OATS: DAnyaBedaH, *owaH (use also for the seed).
OAT , s. owsaMjYakaH SasyaBedaH or DAnyaBedaH.
OAT-MEAL: *owacUrRam or owakzodaH.
OAT-MEAL , s. owsaMjYakaSasyacUrRaM, pUrvvoktaDAnyakzodaH.
OATEN: (1) by comp.;(2) *OwaH (wI, waM); (3) *owamayaH (yI, yaM).
OATEN , a. pUrvvoktaSasyamayaH -yI -yaM, pUrvvoktaDAnyacUrRamayaH &c.
Oath, s. SapaTaH, aBiSApaH, vacanaM, pratijYA, samayaH; ‘bind by an o(ath)’ Sap c.; ‘to take an o(ath)’ Sap 1, 4 U, SapaTaM Sap; ‘with an o(ath)’ saSapaTaM, SapaTapUrvaM.

OATH: (1) SapaTaH, to take an o.: SapaTaM karoti, D.; to bind with an o.: SapaTena niyacCati, N. s.; to administer an o.: SapaTaM SApayati, Mit.; he swore thousand of o.s: sahasraSo'sO SapaTAnaSapyat, B. iii. 32.;(2) divyam. (= special oath; ordeal: q.v.).

OATH , s. SapaTaH, SApaH, SapaH -panaM, aBiSApaH, pariSApaH, divyaM, satyaM, samayaH, pratyayaH, aBIzaNgaH, aBizaNgaH, parigrahaH, kriyA; ‘to take an oath,’ Sap (c. 1. Sapati -te, c. 4. Sazyati -te, SazwuM), aBiSap, SapaTaM [Page540-b+ 51] kf, SapaTaM Sap; ‘he took an oath,’ SapaTaM Sepe; ‘to administer an oath,’ Sap (c. 10. SApayati -yituM); ‘made to take an oath,’ SApitaH -tA -taM; ‘with an oath,’ saSapaTaM, SapaTapUrvvaM, SapaTapuraHsaraM.
OATH-BREAKING (subs.): SapaTamaNgaH: v. Per- -jury.
OATH-BREAKING , s. SapaTaBaNgaH, divyaBaNgaH, miTyASapaTaH, miTyAdivyaM.
OBDURACY: kAWinyam: v. Hardness.
OBDURACY , s. stabDacittatA, cittastabDatA, stabDatA, kaWinacittatvaM, cittakA- WinyaM, kaWinatA, dfQatA, dArQyaM, ananutApaSIlatA, anutApavimuKatA, AgrahaH, AgrahaSIlatA, pApAgrahaH, pApAtyAgaH.
Obdurate, a. anamya, kaWina, kaWinahfdaya-citta, anutApavimuKa (KI f.), durAgraha; See Hard. Obduracy, s. cittakAWinyaM, kaWorahfdayatA, anutApavimuKatA; kAWinyaM, kaWoratA.
OBDURATE: kaWinaH (nA, naM): v. Hard, obsti- -nate.

OBDURATE , a. stabDacittaH -ttA -ttaM, kaWinacittaH &c., dfQacittaH &c., ananutApaSIlaH -lA -laM, anutApavimuKaH -KA -KaM, anutApaparANmuKaH -KA -KaM, durAgrahI -hiRI -hi (n), pApAgrahI &c., pApAtyAgI &c.
OBDURATELY: kaWinam: v. Hardly, obstinately.
OBDURATELY , adv. stabDacittatvAt, kaWinacittatvAt, sakAWinyaM.
OBEDIENCE: AjYAnuvfttiH and sim. comp.s.; (2) vaSyatA.

OBEDIENCE , s. AjYAnuvarttanaM, AjYAnusaraRaM, AjYAkaraRaM, AjYApAlanaM, AjYAnuvfttiH f., AjYAnukUlatA, AjYAnukUlyaM, AjYAgrAhitvaM, AjYADAraRaM, AjYADInatA, AjYAnuroDaH, AjYAsevanaM, AdeSakaraRaM, nideSakaraRaM, AjYAparatA, AjYAnuviDAyitA, vaSatA, vaSyatA, SuSrUzA -zaRaM, anuvarttanaM, anuvfttiH f., anukUlatA, AnukUlyaM, vaSavarttanaM, mAnyatA, AjYAmAnanaM, vaSIBUtatA.

OBEDIENT: (1) AjYAkaraH (rI, raM) and sim. comp.s., your o. servant is exceedingly obliged: so'yamAryeRAjYAkaro jano'tyarTamanugfhItaH, D. vi.;(2) AjYAnuvartin (f. nI) and sim. comp.s.;(3) vaSya (f. SyA) or vaSaga (f. gA), etc. (= submissive).

OBEDIENT , a. AjYAnuvarttI -rttinI -rtti (n), AjYApAlakaH -kA -kaM, AjYADInaH -nA -naM, AjYAnuyAyI &c., AjYAnusArI &c., AjYAkaraH -rI -raM, AjYA- kArI &c., AdeSakArI &c., nideSakArI &c., AdeSakaraH &c., vacana- karaH &c., vacaskaraH &c., AjYAsevI &c., AjYAparaH -rA -raM, anuSA- sanaparaH &c., vaSaH -SA -SaM, vaSyaH -SyA -SyaM, vaSavarttI &c., vaSAnugaH -gA -gaM, SuSrUzuH -zuH -zu, AjYAvahaH -hA -haM, AjYAvAhakaH -kA -kaM, AjYAsampAdakaH &c., AjYAsampAdI &c., AjYADArI &c., anuvarttI &c., anuviDAyI &c., viDAyI &c., anukUlaH -lA -laM, sevI &c., AjYA- grAhI &c., vacanagrAhI &c., nideSagrAhI &c., ASravaH -vA -vaM, aDInaH -nA -naM; ‘obedient to a parent,’ pitfvAkparaH -rA -raM, pitfvaca- nakaraH -rA -raM, pitfvaSaH -SA -SaM, pitfvaSAnugaH &c.
OBEDIENTLY: AjYAyAM tizWat (f. ntI): v. To obey.
OBEDIENTLY , adv. SuSrUzayA, sAnuvarttanaM, AjYAnuvarttanapUrvvaM, sAnukUlyaM, AjYAnusAreRa -ratas, AjYAnuvarttanena, yaTAdizwaM, yaTAdeSaM, yaTAjYaM, yaTAnujYaM.

Obeisance, s. namaskAraH; praRAmaH, praRati f., vaMdanaM, praRipAtaH, namasyA; aBivAdanaM; ‘prostrate o(beisance)’ sAzwAMgapraRAmaH-namaskAraH, azwAMga-pAtaH; ‘to make an o(beisance)’ praRam 1 P, praRipat 1 P, namaskf 8 U, aBivad c.
OBEISANCE: (1) namaskAraH;(2) praRAmaH;(3) praRatiH.

OBEISANCE , s. namaskAraH, praRAmaH, praRatiH f., praRipAtaH, praRipatanaM, namas indecl., namasyA, sannatiH f., natiH f., namanaM, vinayaH, vinItiH f., upasaNgrahaH; ‘from inferiors to superiors,’ aYjaliH m., aYjali- karmma n. (n), aYjalibanDanaM, vandanaM; ‘from a Brahman,’ ASI- rvAdaH; ‘from an inferior to a religious preceptor, Guru, &c.,’ aBivAdanaM, aBivandanaM; ‘from Hindūs of inferior caste,’ daRqavat; ‘to an idol, &c.,’ vandanaM. — (Profound obeisance with all the members of the body) sAzwANgapraRAmaH, sAzwANganamaskAraH, azwANgapAtaH, azwANgapraRAmaH; ‘to make obeisance,’ namaskf, praRam (c. 1. -Ramati -RantuM), SirasA praRam, kAyaM praRam, praRipat (c. 1. -patati -tituM), sAzwANgapAtaM praRipat; ‘having made obeisance,’ praRamya.
Obelisk, s. sUcyAkAraH staMBaH.
OBELISK: perh. stUpaH; *sUcistUpaH.
OBELISK , s. sUcyAkAraH stamBaH, dIrGaprastaramayaH stamBaviSezaH.
OBELIZE: *sUcireKayA cihnayati (cihna, c. 10.).
OBELUS: *sUcireKA.
OBERRATION , s. BramaRaM -RA, pariBramaRaM, paryyawanaM, itastato BramaRaM.
Obese, a. pIna, pIvara, sTUla; See Fat.
OBESE: Bedasvin (f. nI): v. Fat.
OBESE , a. medasvI -svinI -svi (n), pInaH -nA -naM, pIvaraH -rA -raM, sTUlaH -lA -laM, sTUlakAyaH -yA -yaM, mAMsalaH lA -laM.
OBESENESS , OBESITY, s. medasvitA, medovfdDiH f., sTUlatA, pInatA.
OBESITY: medasvitA: v. Fatness, corpulence.

Obey, v. t. (Orders) kf 8 U, anu-zWA 1 P, anuvft 1 A, anuvi-DA 3 U, pA c. (pAlayati), anuruD 4 A, man c., pratigrah 9 P, aByupa-i 2 P or gam 1 P; (persons) vacanaM Sru 5 P, SAsane sTA, AjYAM-vacanaM-anuvft, yaTAdizwaM vi-DA; Sru desid. (SuSrU-zate), upacar 1 P, sev 1 A, upAs 2 A, AjYAM kf or anuruD &c. Obedient, a. AjYAnuvartin, AjYAkara (rI f.), AjYAviDAyin, anuviDAyin, anu-roDin, AjYA-nideSa-kArin, AjYApara, viDeya, vinayagrAhin, vacane sTita, ASrava, vaSya, praReya, vaSAnuga, SuSrUzu, AjYAvacana-grAhin-sevin, AjYADIna; ‘o(bedient) to oneʼs parent’ pitfvaSya, pitfvacanapara. [Obedient]ly, adv. AjYAnusAreRa, yaTAjYaM, yaTAdizwaM, nideSAnu-roDena. Obedience, s. AjYAnuvartanaM-anu-roDaH-anusAraH-anusaraRaM-karaRaM-pAlanaM-sevanaM-DAraRaM, vaSyatA, anuviDAyityaM, SuSrUzA, AjYA-karatvaM, AjYAparatA, anuvartanaM, anuroDaH.

OBEY: to o. one or one's order: AjYAm, nirdeSam, etc. pAlayati, anu-, prati- (pAl, c. 10.), or karoti (kf, c. 8.), or anuvartate (vft, c. 1.), or anuviDatte (DA, c. 3.), or vacanaM SfRoti (Sru, c. 5.), or AjYAyAM etc. tizWati (sTA, c. 1.); to o. laws etc.: anuvartate: v. To follow: v. Also to disobey.

To OBEY , v. a. AjYAm or vacanam anuvft (c. 1. -varttate -rttituM), yaTA- dizwam anuzwA (c. 1. -tizWati -zWAtuM), yaTAjYaptaM viDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM) or kf, Sru in des. (SuSrUzate -zituM), anuviDA in pass. (-DIyate), anuruD in pass. (-ruDyate), sev (c. 1. sevate -vituM), upasev, AjYAM or [Page541-a+ 51] vacanaM pratIz (c. 6. -icCati -ezituM) or sampratIz, upacar (c. 1. -carati -rituM), upAcar, upAs (c. 2. -Aste -AsituM), paryupAs, samupAs, aByupe (c. 2. aByupEti -tuM, rt. i), man (c. 10. mAnayati -yituM), AjYAM pAl (c. 10. pAlayati -yituM) or grah (c. 9. gfhlAti, grahItuM) or pratigrah anukUla (nom. anukUlayati -yituM), upajIv (c. 1. -jIvati -vituM), AjYAnuvarttanaM kf. — (Submit to the control of another) paravaSIBU, paravaSaM gam (c. 1. gacCati, gantuM).
OBEYED , p. p. SuSrUzitaH -tA -taM, yaTAdizwam anuzWitaH -tA -taM or vihitaH -tA -taM, mAnitaH -tA -taM, paryupAsitaH -tA -taM, sevitaH -tA -taM.
OBFUSCATE: viklavIkaroti: v. To bewilder.
To OBFUSCATE , v. a. malinIkf, timira (nom. timirayati -yituM), timi- rIkf, kaluzIkf, malina (nom. malinayati -yituM).
OBFUSCATED , p. p. malinIkftaH -tA -taM, timirIkftaH &c., kaluzIkftaH &c.
OBFUSCATION: I Lit.: v. To darken.II Bewilderment: q.v.: vEklavyam.
OBFUSCATION , s. kaluzIkaraRaM, malinIkaraRaM, nizpraBatA, sAnDakAratA.
Obit, s. See ‘Death’. [Obit]uary, a. mftyu-saMbaMDin. s. mftyuleKaH.
OBIT , s. mftakriyA, mftakarmma n. (n), antyakarmma n. See OBSEQUIES.
OBITUARY: *mftyunirdeSaH; maraRolleKaH.
OBITUARY , s. (List of the dead) mftasaMKyApatraM, mftaparisaMKyA, mftanA- mAvalipatraM. — (Account of the dead) mftavarRanaM -nA, mftacaritraM, mftavivaraRaM.

Object, s. dravyaM, vastu n., arTaH, vizayaH, iMdri-yArTaH; ‘visible o(bject)’ cakzurvizayaH; (fig.) pAtraM, padaM, sTAnaM, AspadaM, BAjanaM, BUmi f., vizayaH; ‘o(bject) of contidence’ viSvAsAspadaM, viSvAsaBUmiH; ‘the sole o(bject) of my affection’ snehasyEkAyanIBUtA (M. 2); ‘o(bject) of dispute’ vivAdavizayaH, vyavahArAspadaM. 2 arTaH, PalaM, hetuH; (‘desired o(bject)’) aBIzwaM, izwaM, samIhitaM, kAMkzitaM, IpsitaM, kAmaH, mano-raTaH; See Desire. 3 nimittaM, kAraRaM, prayo-janaM, kAryaM. 4 aBiprAyaH, ASayaH, tAtparyaM, uddeSaH, lakzyaM; ‘with what o(bject) in view’ kimapekzya PalaM, kena hetunA, kimuddiSya, kiM-nimittaM, kimarTaM; ‘accomplishment of oneʼs o(bject)’ kftArTatA, caritArTatA, izwasidDi f., PalaprApti f.; ‘highest o(bject)’ paramArTaH; ‘o(bject) of hearing’ SrutivizayaH. 5 karman n.; ‘a root governing two o(bject)s’ dvikarmakaH DAtuH. v. vi-prati-ruD 7 U, bAD 1 A, KaMq 10, niras 4 U, aDarIkf 8 U, apavad 1 A, na anumana 4 A or anumud 1 A, dozaM grah 9 U, ‘the sage will not o(bject) to this’ nAtra dozaM grahIzyati kulapatiH (S. 3); ni-prati-ziD 1 P, (tadeza sargaH na BavadBiH pratizeDanIyaH R. xiv. 42); in discussions gen. ex. by nanu, iti cet or kaTaM tarhi, followed by ucyate or atrocyate (we reply); pratyavasTA 1 A, vitaMq 1 A. [Object]ion, s. bADaH-DA, apavAdaH, viroDaH, A-kzepaH, dozaH, Apatti f., kakzA, udgrAhaH, virudDahetuH, vipratizeDaH, pratyavAyaH, pratibaMDaH, paryudAsaH, ‘making an o(bjection)’ dozagrahaRaM, viroDopanyAsaH; ‘settling an o(bjection)’ samA-pratisamA-DAnaM, AkzepaparihAraH. [Object]ionable, a. bADya, sabADa, sadoza, nizeDArha, varjya, parihArya, ASaMkanIya. [Object]ive, a. vizayASrita, padArTanizWa, karmavizayaka. [Object]or, s. bADakaH, apavAdakaH.

OBJECT (subs.): I As opposed to subject: vizayaH, of the o. and the subject: vizayavizayiRoH, S.II. An external thing:(1) dravyam, an o. does not destroy its cause or effect: na dravyaM kAryaM kAraRaYca vaDati, V. d.;(2) vastu (n.), for external o.s: bAhyavastuzu, Ku. Ph.: an o. of sense: indriyArTaH, V. d.; an o. of hearing: SrotragrahaRo'rTaH, V. d.III An o. of emotion or effort:(1) pAtram, I was the o. of (their) looks: ahamaBUvaM pAtra- mAlokitAnAm, Ma.; (proper) and improper o.: pAtramapAtraM vA, Mal.;(2) BAjanam, o. of love: praRaya- BAjanam;(3) sTAnam and sim. words (= place), excellencies are o.s of adoration: guRAH pUjAsTAnam, U. iv. 11.; o. of trust: viSvAsaBUmiH, H.; (4) with become, by circumlo., becomes an o. of hatred among the people: dvezyatAM yAti loke, P.: v. To become.IV Aim, intention: (1) prayojanam: without some o.: nizprayojanam, Mu.; (2) arTaH, this o. is io be accomplished with ano- ther o.: arTo'yamarTAntaramAvya eva, Ku.; and with this o.: etadarTaYca, Vi.;(3) aBiprAyaH (= intention), but I, understanding his o.: ahantu viditAmiprAyA, K.V. In gram.: karman (n.), without distin- guishing o. and subject: aviSizwakartfkarmamAvam, An.; taking two o. s: dvikarmakaH, S. k.

OBJECT (v.): I In gen.: expr. by verbs aBiDatte (DA, c. 3.), etc. (= to say) or manyate (man, c. 4.), etc. (= to think) and adj.s BrAnta (f. ntA), asaNgata (f. tA), aprAmARika (f. kI), etc.II To expose: vivfRoti (vf, c. 5.).

OBJECT , s. (That about which any power or faculty is em- ployed, or by which something is presented to the mind) vizayaH, arTaH, indriyArTaH, gocaraH, pAtraM, BAjanaM, BUmiH f., AspadaM, sTAnaM. The first four of these words refer properly to objects of sense, of which five are given, viz. ‘form,’ rUpaM; ‘sound,’ SabdaH; ‘odour,’ ganDaH; ‘flavor,’ rasaH; ‘touch,’ sparSaH. The other words are used elegantly in composi- tion, thus, ‘an object of confidence,’ viSvAsapAtraM, viSvAsaBUmiH f., viSvAsAspadaM, viSvAsasTAnaM; ‘of affection,’ snehaBUmiH f., prItipAtraM; ‘of favor,’ prasAdaBUmiH f.; ‘of compassion,’ kfpApAtraM, dayABAjanaM; ‘of disgrace,’ aBiBavAspadaM; ‘of blame,’ nindApAtraM, nindAvizayaH; ‘of praise,’ stutiBAjanaM; ‘of honor,’ mAnaBAjanaM; ‘of charity or liberality,’ dAnapAtraM; ‘of dispute or litigation,’ vyavahA- ravizayaH, vyavahArasTAnaM; ‘of taxation,’ SulkasTAnaM; ‘deserving object of charity, &c.,’ supAtraM, pAtraM; ‘undeserving,’ kupAtraM, apAtraM; ‘visible object,’ cakzurvizayaH. — (Purpose, end, that to which the mind is directed) aBiprAyaH, ASayaH, aBipretaM, arTaH, vizayaH, uddeSaH, tAtparyyaM, kAryyaM, kAryyavastu n., prayojanaM, prayogaH, aBisanDiH m., prArTitaM, izwaM, padArTaH, lakzaM, lakzyaM, hetuH m., nimittaM, agraBUmiH; ‘accomplishment of one's object,’ svArTasidDiH f., kAryyasidDiH f., izwasidDiH f., kftArTatA, caritArTatA, izwApattiH f., ASA- prAptiH f.; ‘one who has accomplished his object,’ kftArTaH -rTA -rTaM, caritArTaH &c., prAptArTaH &c., kftakftyaH -tyA -tyaM, ASAprAptaH -ptA -ptaM; ‘I have gained my object,’ kftArTo'smi, caritArTo'smi; ‘one's own private object or end,’ svArTaH, svahitaM, svasADanaM; ‘highest object,’ paramArTaH; ‘important object,’ gurvarTaH; ‘the four objects of human pursuit collectively,’ caturvargaH, caturBadraM; these are ‘virtue,’ DarmmaH; ‘wealth,’ arTaH; ‘love,’ kAmaH; ‘final beatitude,’ mokzaH; ‘the three objects without the last,’ trivargaH, trigaRaM; ‘with what object,’ kimarTaM, kimuddiSya. — (In grammar) karmma n. (n), karmmapadaM.

KaRqayati -yituM), vyAGAtaM kf, ApattiM kf.
OBJECTED TO , p. p. paryyudastaH -stA -staM, apavAditaH -tA -taM, asvIkftaH -tA -taM.
OBJECTION: (1) prativAdaH (?);(2) ApattiH (used in Bengali);(3) bADA (= obstruction. obstacle);(4) by verb.

OBJECTION , s. bADA -DaH -DakaM, virudDahetuH m., bADArTakahetuH m., viro- DArTakahetuH m., virudDavacanaM, udgrAhaH, kakzA, apavAdaH, SaNkA, ASaNkA, apavAdaH, viparItavacanaM, vAkyaKaRqanaM, vAkyaviroDaH, vyAGAtaH, pratibanDaH, ApattiH f., vipratipattiH f., pratyavAyaH, vitaRqA, AkzepaH, paryyudAsaH; ‘making an objection,’ virudDahetuvAdaH, kakzAvAdaH; ‘settling an objection,’ samADiH m., samADAnaM.
OBJECTIONABLE: duzwaH (zwA, zwaM), asaNgataH (tA, taM), etc.

OBJECTIONABLE , a. bADyaH -DyA -DyaM, bADanIyaH -yA -yaM, sabADaH -DA -DaM, pariharaRIyaH -yA -yaM, parihAryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM, varjanIyaH -yA -yaM, varjyaH -rjyA -rjyaM, apavAdyaH -dyA -dyaM, sadozaH -zA -zaM, pratizeDArhaH -rhA -rhaM, nizeDArhaH &c., SaNkanIyaH -yA -yaM, ASaNkanIyaH &c., pratibanDArhaH &c.; ‘objectionable person or thing,’ parihAraH.
OBJECTIONABLENESS , s. bADyatA, sabADatvaM, bADaH, sadozatA.

OBJECTIVE , a. (Pertaining to the object) svADArasTitaH -tA -taM, svADAranizWaH -zWA -zWaM, vizayASritaH -tA -taM, vizayanizWaH &c., padArTASritaH -tA -taM, vizayasambanDI -nDinI &c., pAtranizWaH &c., pAtrasambanDI &c. — (In grammar) karmmapadavizayaH -yA -yaM.
OBJECTIVELY: expr. by adj. vizayagataH (tA, taM). (?).
OBJECTOR , s. bADakaH, virudDahetuvAdI m. (n), kakzAvAdI, apavAdakaH.
Objuration, s. SapaTaH.

Objurgate, v. t. niMd 1 P, Barts 10 A, upAlaB 1 A, A-aDi-kzip 6 P, tiraskf 8 U. [Objurgat]ion, s. niMdA, BartsanaM-nA, upAlaMBaH, AkzepaH, DikkAraH; See Censure. [Objurgat]ory, a. niMdaka, niMdArTaka.
OBJURGATE: Bartsayati (Barts, c. 10.): v. To reprove.

To OBJURGATE , v. a. nind (c. 1. nindati -ndituM), upAlaB (c. 1. -laBate -labDuM), AkruS (c. 1. -kroSati -krozwuM), samAkruS Barts (c. 10. Bartsayate -ti -yituM), kzip (c. 6. kzipati, kzeptuM), avakzip, Akzip, aDikzip, Dikkf.
OBJURGATION: BartsanA: v. Reproof.
OBJURGATION , s. nindA, upAlamBaH, tiraskAraH, BartsanavAkyaM, nirBartsanaM, kzepaH, avakzepaH, DikkAraH, parIvAdaH.
OBJURGATORY , a. nindakaH -kA -kaM, nindArTakaH -kA -kaM, tiraskArArTakaH &c.
OBLATE: in geo.: *avanataH (tA, taM).

Oblation, s. baliH, upahAraH, upAyanaM; havyaM, havanaM, hutaM, Ahuti f., izwi f., yAgaH, nirvapaRaM; ‘o(blation) of eatables’ nEvedyaM; ‘o(blation) to all deities’ vESvadevaH; ‘to make o(blation)s to fire’ hu 3 P.
OBLATION: (1) baliH, offer o.s to the (divine) mothers: mAtfByo balimupahara, Mr. i.;(2) nEvedyam (of uncooked rice, sweetmeats etc.);(3) havyam (in fire, gen. of ghee);(4) kavyam (to the manes).

OBLATION , s. (Offering to the gods, &c.) baliH m., upahAraH, devopahAraH, upaharaRaM, hutaM, havyaM, homaH, hutahomaM, AhutiH f., AhavaH -vanaM, havanaM, upAyanaM, devopAyanaM, kavyaM, nirvapaRaM, avadAnaM, satraM, caruH m., prayAgaH, izwiH f., vEtAnaM, vitAnaH -naM, savaH, pAtrIraH, kuRqapAyyaH. — (Of eatable articles, &c.) nEvedyaM, nivedanaM. — (Of curds) pfzadAjyaM. — (Of rice-milk and sugar) paramAnnaM, pAyasaH. — (A respectful oblation of rice, &c. with water) arGyaM, arGaH; ‘the presen- tation of it,’ arDadAnaM. — (Oblation to all the deities) vESvadevaM, vESvadevakarmma n. — (To the manes) kavyaM. See MANES. (To the gods and manes) havyakavyaM; ‘dressed oblation,’ havyapAkaH; ‘grand and extraordinary oblation,’ mahAbaliH m., mahAnEvedyaM; ‘proper for an oblation,’ havyaH -vyA -vyaM; ‘to make an oblation to fire,’ anale homaM kf.
OBLECTATION , s. AnandaH, AhlAdaH, harzaH, pramodaH, madaH.
To OBLIGATE , v. a. banD (c. 9. baDnAti, bandDuM), nibanD, badDaM -dDAM -dDaM kf, niyamena banD, niyamapUrvvaM or pratijYApUrvvaM, banD.

OBLIGATION: I Binding moral power:(1) banDaH (= bond);(2) DarmaH (= duty).II A contract: q.v.: saMvid (f.).III Indebted- -ness: under o. expr. by fRin (f, nI) (= indebted), or upakftaH (tA, taM) (= done [Page481] good to) or anugfhItaH (tA, taM) (= favoured) or badDa (f. dDA), his generosity lay the whole vill- age under o.: *grAmaH samagrastasya dayAlutayA badDaH.

OBLIGATION , s. (Binding power, as of a vow, promise, debt, &c., incumbency) avaSyakatA -tvaM, AvaSyakatA, avaSyakarttavyatA -tvaM, avaSyakAryyatA, karttavyatA, viDeyatA, avaSyamBAvaH, AvaSyaM, BAraH, fRaM; ‘under the obligation of a debt,’ fRI -RinI -Ri (n); ‘free from obligation,’ afRI &c., avatIrRarRaH -rRA -rRaM, uttIrRaH [Page542-a+ 51] &c., fRamuktaH -ktA -ktaM; ‘religious obligation,’ vrataM, yamaH, niyamaH, vizayaH; ‘under a religious obligation,’ vratI &c., vratasTaH -sTA -sTaM; ‘observing or taking on one's self a religious obligation,’ vratAcaraRaM, vratasaNgrahaH; ‘violating it,’ vratalopaH -panaM. — (Engagement, compact) niyamaH, samayaH, pratijYA -jYAnaM, saMvid f., saMskAraH, upagamaH, aByupagamaH, aByupAyaH, sanDA, sanDAnaM, sanDiH m., saMSravaH. — (Bound state) badDatA, nibadDatA. — (Favor, any act by which a person becomes bound to another) upakAraH, anugrahaH, upakftaM, sukftaM, hitaM, priyaM, upacAraH, kftopakAraH; ‘to lay under an obligation,’ upakf, upakAreRa badDaM -dDAM kf, upakArabadDaM -dDAM kf.
OBLIGATORY: expr. with avaSyam (= must: q.v.).

OBLIGATORY , a. avaSyakaH -kA -kaM, AvaSyakaH -kI -kaM, avaSyakarttavyaH -vyA -vyaM, avaSyaH -SyA -SyaM, avaSyakAryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM, avaSyamantavyaH -vyA -vyaM, avaSyamAnanIyaH -yA -yaM, avaSyapAlanIyaH -yA -yaM.

Oblige, v. t. Ex. by causal of verbs, gen. with balena or balAt; prayuj 10, pravft c.; See Compel. 2 niyamapUrvaM-sapra-tijYaM baMD 9 P. 3 anugrah 9 P, upakf 8 U, upakAreRa baMD, hitaM-prasAdaM-upakAraM kf; ‘I am much o(blig)ed to you for this reward’ etena pAritozikadAnena BavatA sutarAmupakf-tosmi-anugfhItosmi; ‘I am much o(blig)ed’ anugfhItosmi, mahAnayaM prasAdaH. [Oblig]ation, s. avaSyakatA, kartavyatA, BAraH, fRaM, baMDaH, DarmaH; ‘free from the o(bligation)s of debt’ fRamukta, muktarRa, anfRa; ‘religious o(bligation)’ vrataM, niyamaH, codanA, viDiH. 2 saMvid f., samayaH, pratijYA, niyamaH, aByupagamaH, saMDA, saM-A-SravaH. 3 anugrahaH, upakAraH, upakfti f. -taM, hitaM, priyaM; ‘under o(bligation)’ upakfta-anugfhIta a.; ‘my o(bligation)s to you are immense’ tava mayi upakArAH saM-KyAtItAH; ‘to lay under o(bligation)s’ upakf; See (v.). [Oblig]atory, a. avaSyaka AvaSyaka (kI f.), aparihArya, avaSyakartavya; oft. ex. by avaSyaM; See under Compel. [Oblig]ing, a. anugraha-upakAra-SIla, upakArin, anugrAhin, hita-upakAra-budDi, suSIla, dakziRa, anukUla, sujana. [Oblig]ingly, adv. dAkziRyena, sujana-tayA, sAnugrahaM, suSIlavat. [Oblig]ingness, s. upakAra-anugraha-SIlaM, sOjanyaM.
OBLIGE: I To bind: baDnAti (banD, c. 9.). II To compel: q.v. O. d. = under obli- -gation: v. Obligation (III).

To OBLIGE , v. a. (Constrain, compel). Expressed by the causal form usually in conjunction with balAt or balena or balAtkAreRa; as, ‘to oblige a man to do any thing,’ balena puruzaM kiYcit kf in caus. (kArayati -yituM) or pravft in caus. (-varttayati -yituM); ‘to oblige to pay,’ dA in caus. (dApayati -yituM); ‘to oblige to go,’ balena gam (c. 10. gamayati -yituM); ‘he obliged me to take the book,’ SAstraM mAM grAhayAmAsa. The root arh is sometimes used in this sense. See To COMPEL. (Bind) banD (c. 9. baDnAti, bandDuM), nibanD. — (By a compact or agree- ment) niyamena or niyamapUrvvaM or pratijYApUrvvaM banD. — (By a favor or kindness) upakAreRa banD or badDaM -dDAM kf, upakArabadDaM -dDAM kf. — (Favor, do a favor to) anugrah (c. 9. -gfhlAti -grahItuM), anugrahaM kf, anuruD (c. 4. -ruDyati -te -rodDuM), upakf, upakAraM kf, sAhAyyaM kf, hitaM kf, priyaM kf; ‘to be obliged.’ See the next.

OBLIGED , p. p. (Compelled) expressed by the pass. part. of the causal form. See COMPELLED, CONSTRAINED. (Bound) badDaH -dDA -dDaM; ‘by a favor,’ upakArabadDaH &c. — (Favored, in- debted) anugfhItaH -tA -taM, upakftaH -tA -taM; ‘I am obliged to you for your advice,’ anugfhIto'smi or anugfhIto'haM tavopadeSena.
OBLIGING (adj.): dakziRa (f. RA): v. Also kind, good-natured.

OBLIGING , a. (Having the disposition to do favors) upakAraSIlaH -lA -laM, upakArI -riRI -ri (n), paropakArI &c., upakArabudDiH -dDiH -dDi, anugrAhI &c., anuroDI &c., anukUlaH -lA -laM, priyaNkaraH -rA -raM, muSIlaH -lA -laM.
OBLIGINGLY: dAkziRyena: v. Also liberally.
OBLIGINGLY , adv. upakAraSIlatvAt, upakArabudDyA, sAnugrahaM, anugraheRa, anuroDena, sAnukUlyaM, prItyA, suSIlavat, muSIlatvAt.
OBLIGINGNESS: dAkziRyam: v. Kindness, civility.
OBLIGINGNESS , s. upakAraSIlatA, paropakAraSIlatA, paropakAritA, anu- grahaH, anugrahaSIlatA, anuroDaH, anukUlatA, AnukUlyaM, suSIlatA.

Oblique, a. vakra, kuwila, jihma, asarala, tiryac, anfju, vizama; ‘o(blique) speech’ va-krokti f., BaMgi-gI f., uparoDavacanaM; ‘o(blique) case’ apraDAnakArakaM. [Oblique]ly, adv. vakraM, kuwilaM, tiryak, tiraH, sAci, jihmaM. [Oblique]ness, s. vakratA, kOwilyaM, anfjutA, vEzamyaM; ‘o(bliqueness) of sight’ vakradfzwi f., dfzwivakratA; ‘o(bliqueness) of conduct’ vimArga-utpaTa-gamanaM, asadAcAraH, satpaTa-BraMSaH-tyAgaH.
OBLIQUE: vakra (f. krA), o. line: vakrareKA; o. insinuation: vakroktiH; o. speech: *kaTakasya i. e. teller's (in opposition to vaktuH = speaker's i. e. direct) uktiH; o. case: apraDAnakArakam.

OBLIQUE , a. (Not direct) vakraH -krA -kraM, vakrimaH -mA -maM, kuwilaH -lA -laM, jihmaH -hmA -hmaM, vijihmaH &c., tiryaN -raScI -ryak (c), asaralaH -lA -laM, anfjuH -juH -ju, vakrI -kriRI -kri (n), vizamaH -mA -maM, — (As language, &c.) vakraH -krA -kraM, aspazwaH -zwA -zwaM, uparoDI &c.; ‘oblique speech,’ vakroktiH f., vakraBaRitaM. — (In grammar) kAra- kaviBaktikaH -kA -kaM; ‘oblique case,’ kArakaM, kArakaviBaktiH f., kArakaM. — (Oblique vision) vakradfzwiH f.; ‘having it,’ vakradfzwiH zwiH -zwi, tiryagdfzwiH &c.
OBLIQUELY: vakram: v. Askance.
OBLIQUELY , adv. vakraM, kuwilaM, tiryak, tiras, jihmaM, vijihmaM, asaralaM.
OBLIQUENESS: Obliquity. I Lit.: vakratA: v. Crookedness.II Deviation: natiH.III Fig., iniquity: q.v.: vakratA.

OBLIQUENESS , OBLIQUITY, s. vakratA, kuwilatA, kOwilyaM, jihmatA, tiryaktvaM, asaralatA, asAralyaM, anfjutA -tvaM, vizamatA; ‘of vision,’ vakradfzwiH f., [Page542-b+ 51] dfzwivakratA, vakradfzwitvaM, tiryagdfzwitvaM. — (Deviation from moral rectitude) vimArgagamanaM, vipaTagamanaM, utpaTagamanaM, kapaTagamanaM, satpaTa- BraMSaH, satpaTatyAgaH, asadAcAraH, vyaBicAraH.
Obliterate, v. t. vi-, lup 6 P or c., pra-pari-ava-mfj 2 P or c., vyAmfS 6 P or c., vi-naS c., ucCid 7 P, unmUl 10. [Obliterat]ion, s. lopaH, mArjanaM, vyAmarSaH, ucCedaH.
OBLITERATE: (1) lumpati, vi-, A-, ava- (lup, c. 6.), my sight is o.d: dfzwirAlupyate me, Me. ii. 44.; (2) mArzwi, pari-, pra-, apa- (Bfj, c. 2.): To erase.

To OBLITERATE , v. a. apamfj (c. 2. -mArzwi -rzwuM), vyAmfj, pramfj, avamfj, vyAmfS (c. 6. -mfSati -mrazwuM), avamfS, vyAmarzaM kf, avamarzaRaM kf, ucCid (c. 7. -Cinatti -CettuM), lup (c. 6. lumpati, loptuM), lopaM kf, vinaS (c. 10. -nASayati -yituM), unmUl (c. 10. -mUlayati -yituM); ‘is oblite- rated from the memory,’ vismAryyate.
OBLITERATED , p. p. apamfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, vyAmfzwaH &c., unmfzwaH &c., ucCinnaH -nnA -nnaM, luptaH -ptA -ptaM, vitIrRaH -rRA -rRaM.
OBLITERATION: (1) lopaH, vi-, ava-, A-;(2) mArjanA.
OBLITERATION , s. mArjanA, apamArjanA, vyAmarzaH, avamarzaRaM, lopaH.
Oblivion, s. a-vi-smfti f., a-vi-smaraRaM; ‘to bury into o(blivion)’ vismf 1 P. 2 doza-vismaraRaM. Oblivious, a. smftihara (rI f.), vismAraka, vismftikara (rI f.). 2 vismaraRaSIla.
OBLIVION: vismftiH: v. Forgetfulness.
OBLIVION , s. vismftiH f., vismaraRaM, asmftiH f., asmaraRaM, smftinASaH, smftihAniH f., vyAmohaH. — (Remission of offences) dozavismaraRaM, sakalAparADamocanaM.
OBLIVIOUS: I Causing oblivion: smftimuz (mfn.), smftiharaH (rI, raM) and sim. comp.s. II Forgetful: q.v.
OBLIVIOUS , a. (Causing forgetfulness) vismArakaH -kA -kaM, vismfti- janakaH -kA -kaM, vismftikArakaH &c. — (Forgetful) vismaraRaSIlaH -lA -laM.
OBLIVIOUSNESS , s. vismaraRaSIlatA, vismftiH f. See FORGETFULNESS.
Oblong, a. dIrGAkAra, Ayata, dIrGacaturasra. s. AyataH.
OBLONG: I Adj.: AyataH (tA, taM).II Subs.: AyataH, Li.
OBLONG , a. AyataH -tA -taM, AyatimAn -matI -mat (t), dIrGacaturasraH -srA -sraM, dIrGacaturasrAkAraH -rA -raM, dIrGAkAraH &c.
OBLONG , a. (The figure) AyataH -taM, dIrGacaturasraH -sraM.
Obloquy, s. niMdA, pari(rI)vAdaH, apavAdaH; vAcyatA, BartsanA, garhA; See Censure, Calumny.
OBLOQUY: pari(rI)vAdaH: v. Censure, reproach.
OBLOQUY , s. nindA, parIvAdaH, pariBAzaRaM, apavAdaH, nindoktiH f., paruzo- ktiH f., durvAkyaM, duruktaM, vAcyatA, tiraskAraH.
OBMUTESCENCE , s. mOnaM, aBAzaRaM, vAkstamBaH, vAgroDaH, gatavAktvaM.

Obnoxious, a. vaSa, aDIna, Ayatta, yogya, arha; pAtraM, AspadaM, vizayaH in comp.; ex. by pot. pass. part.; See Liable, Apt. 2 garhita, dvezya, dvezaRIya, garhya; anizwa, apriya, niMdya, aprItikara (rI f.). [Obnoxious]ly, adv. apriyaM, garhyatayA. [Obnoxious]ness, s. aDInatA, vaSatA, pAtratA. 2 dvezyatA, garhyatA.
OBNOXIOUS: I Liable, subject: q.v.: -vaSaH (SA, SaM) in comp.II Offensive, hateful: q.v.: garhitaH (tA, taM).

OBNOXIOUS , a. (Liable, subject) yogyaH -gyA -gyaM, aDInaH -nA -naM, vaSaH -SA -SaM, arhaH -rhA -rhaM, upayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, pAtra in comp., Aspada in comp., vizaya in comp., aDikArI -riRI &c.; ‘obnoxious to punishment,’ daRqayogyaH &c., daRqyaH -RqyA -RqyaM, daRqanIyaH -yA -yaM, daRqArhaH -rhA -rhaM; ‘to disease,’ rogADInaH -nA -naM, rogapAtraM, rogAspadaM; ‘to death,’ maraRADInaH &c., maraRapAtraM; ‘to blame,’ nindAvizayaH -yA -yaM. — (Odious, offensive) dvezyaH -zyA -zyaM, dvezaRIyaH -yA -yaM, dvezI &c., apriyaH -yA -yaM, vipriyaH &c., anizwaH -zwA -zwaM, asantozakaraH -rA -raM, aprItikaraH &c.
OBNOXIOUSLY , adv. dvezaRIyaM, apriyaM, vipriyaM, vyalIkaM, virudDaM.
OBNOXIOUSNESS , s. (Liability) yogyatA, aDInatA, vaSatA. — (Odious- ness) dvezyatA, dvezaRIyatA, apriyatA, anizwatA.
OBOLUS: *ElenaH kzudrarUpyamudrAviSezaH; OpalaH.

Obscene, a. aSlIla, grAmya, anakzara, avAcya, garhya, kutsita, durukta, bIBatsa, aSrAvya, viyAta, vrIqAvaha. 2 aSuBa, aBadra, amaMgala, alakzaRa. [Obscene]ly, adv. aSlIlaM, avAcyaM. [Obscen]ity, [Obscene]ness, s. aSlIlatA, avAcyatA; ‘o(bscenity) of language’ durukti f., durvAkyaM.

OBSCENE: I In gen.:(1) aSlIlaH (lA, laM) (= indecent: q.v.);(2) vrIqAkaraH (rI, raM) and sim. comp.s (lit. = producing shame), Sah.(3) viyAtaH (tA, taM) (= immodest); (4) nyaNgasaMyutaH (tA, taM) (in low abuse), Mit. II Ill-omened: amaNgalaH (lA, laM) and sim. comp.s.

OBSCENE , a. avAcyaH -cyA -cyaM, garhyaH -rhyA -rhyaM, garhitaH -tA -taM, aSudDaH -dDA -dDaM, avacanIyaH -yA -yaM, anakzaraH -rA -raM, apavitraH -trA -traM, kutsitaH -tA -taM, bIBatsaH -tsA -tsaM, duruktaH -ktA -ktaM, kuSrAvyaH -vyA -vyaM; ‘obscene word,’ apaSabdaH, durvacanaM. — (Ill-omened) aSuBaH -BA -BaM, amaNgalaH -lA -laM, aBadraH -drA -draM, amaNgalasUcakaH -kA -kaM.
OBSCENELY: (1) aSlIlam (acc.);(2) often by comp.
OBSCENELY , adv. avAcyaM, garhitaM, garhaRIyaM, aSudDaM, kutsitaM.
OBSCENENESS , OBSCENITY, s. avAcyatA, garhyatA, aSudDatA -tvaM, kutsitatvaM, bIBatsatA; ‘of language,’ durvacanaM, durvAkyaM, durBAzaRaM, duruktiH f., apaSabdaH.
OBSCENITY: I The state:(1) aSlIlatA;(2) vrIqAkaratA.II Anything obscene: expr. by adj.
OBSCURATION: (1) AcCAdanam;(2) AvaraRam, for o. of sight: AvaraRAya dfzweH, R. v. 18.;(3) uparoDaH, R.

OBSCURATION , s. (Act) kaluzIkaraRaM, timirIkaraRaM, malinIkaraRaM, prakA- SaharaRaM, kAntiharaRaM. — (State) nizpraBatA, sAnDakAratA, tejaHkzayaH, tejohAniH f., praBAkzayaH, prakASakzayaH. — (Of a planet) astaH -staM.

Obscure, a. tamovfta, sAMDakAra, nizpraBa, malina, satimira, nistejas, tamasvin. 2 aprasidDa, nAtiviSruta, avijYAta, aKyAta, alpakIrti, laGupratizWa. 3 ni-, gUQa, durboDa, klizwa, durjYeya, gahana, durgama, vizama, aprakASa, aspazwa, asPuwa, gUQArTa, avyakta. v. t. (tamasA) pra-A-cCad 10, Avf 5 U, uparuD 7 U, aMtarayati (D.), malinI-timirI-kf 8 U, malinayati-timirayati- (D.), praBAM-tejaH-hf 1 P or kzi 1, 5 P; ‘o(bscure) with clouds’ meGEH AcCad or Avf. 2 gahanIkf, gUQIkf; ex. by (a.). 3 (Fig.) pratyA-diS 6 P, pratyAKyA 2 P, pracCad; See Eclipse. ‘o(bscur)er of Śri’ pratyAdeSaH SriyaH (V. 1). [Obscur]ation, s. malinIkaraRaM, kAMti-praBA-haraRaM. 2 tejaH or praBA-kzayaH or hAni f., nizpraBatA, sAMDakAratA. [Obscur]ed, a. tamovfta, nazwa-kzIRa-malina-kzata-praBa-kAMti-prakASa, malina, nistejas, hatajyotis. (t), sarasvAn m. (t), ratnAkaraH, pArAvAraH, pArApAraH, dUrapAraH, akUpAraH, dvIpavAn m. (t), mahAkacCaH, DaraRIplavaH, tarIzaH, stimBiH m., DenaH, daBraH, mIraH, tIrTarAjaH; ‘the southern ocean,’ dakziRArRavaH; ‘ocean-bound,’ sAgarAntaH -ntA -ntaM, samudrameKalaH -lA -laM, samudravalayaH -yA -yaM, samudra- rasanaH -nA -naM, arRavameKalaH &c.; ‘ocean-king,’ jalaniDinATaH; ‘ocean of trouble,’ duHKasAgaraH; ‘of business,’ kAryyAbDiH m.; ‘of misery.’ vyasanArRavaH. Seven oceans are fabled to exist by the Hindūs, viz. ‘the ocean of salt,’ lavaRodaH; ‘of syrup or sugar-cane juice,’ ikzurasodaH; ‘of spirituous liquor,’ surodaH; ‘of ghee or clarified butter,’ GftodaH; ‘of milk,’ kzIrodaH; ‘of curds,’ daDyudaH; ‘of pure water,’ SudDodaH; ‘churning of the ocean,’ samudramanTanaM. The mountain mandaraH is fabled to have been used by the Suras and Asuras in the churn- ing of the ocean after the deluge, for the recovery or production of fourteen sacred things. These were, 1. ‘the goddess Lakṣmī,’ lakzmIH, 2. ‘the jewel of Krishna,’ kOstuBaH, 3. ‘the tree of paradise,’ pArijAtaH, 4. ‘spirituous liquor personified as a nymph,’ surA -rI, 5. ‘the physician of the gods,’ DanvantariH m., 6. ‘the moon,’ candraH, 7. ‘the cow of plenty,’ kAmaDenuH f., kAmaduGA, kAmaDuk f. (-duh), 8. ‘the elephant of Indra,’ ErAvataH, 9. ‘the horse of Indra,’ uccEH- SravAH m. (s), 10. ‘nymph of Indra's heaven,’ apsarAH f. (s), [Page546-b+ 51] apsarA, 11. ‘a deadly poison,’ vizaM, halAhalaH -laM, hAlahAlaM, hAlahalaM, kAlakUwaH -waM, 12. ‘nectar or ambrosia,’ amftaM, 13. ‘Indra's bow,’ indraDanus, 14. ‘conch,’ SaNKaH. The mountain Mandara is also called indrakIlaH.

Of, prep. Gen. ex. by genitive or by comp.; ‘o(f) great strength’ mahAbala. 2 (Showing reference) aDikftya, uddiSya (with acc.), or by gata in comp.; ‘by thinking o(f) her husband’ BartfgatayA ciMtayA. 3 (Made of) by Tat. comp. or maya (yI f.), nirmita in comp.; or by derivatives; ‘pot o(f) gold’ hema-pAtraM, hemamayaM or hEmaM pAtraM. 4 (Partitive sense) by gen. or loc., or maDye, maDyAt with gen. 5 (Apposition) ex. by comp. or by nAma ind.; ‘the island o(f) Ceylon’ siMhaladvIpaM, siMhalaM nAma dvIpaM. 6 (Showing cause) by instr. or abl.; ‘died o(f) fever’ jvareRa mftaH.

OF: I Denoting relation: expr. by gen. or tat. comp., daughter of the king of Kāsi: kASirAjaputrI, V.; speed of a chariot: raTasya vegaH, Sa.; conquest of Tripura: tripuravijayaH, Me. N. B. (a) do not use gen. when one subs. is in apposition with another: all of us: sarve vayam, K.; entered the city of Oudh: puramaviSada- yoDyAm, R.; the island of Ceylon: siMhaladvIpaH, Kar.; in the m. of Fālguna or Chaitra: PAlgune cEtre vA mAsi, K. b.; (b) expr. by an adj. or bah. when it introduces an attributive clause, a man of wealth: DanI; of great strength: mahAbalaH (lA, laM); of many kinds: nAnAviDaH (DA, DaM); (c) expr. by a deriv. when it indicates a man's abode: a man of Oudh: AyoDyikaH, U.; nobody of this place: na kaScidihatyaH, D.: v. Inhabitant; (d) part. in uka (except kAmuka) take an acc., killer of demons: dEtyAn GAtukaH, S. k.II About, con- -cerning: q.v.: expr. by gen., what would one say of the other: kiM BaRatveka ekasya, Sa.; do you remember of your master: kaccidBartuH smarasi, Me.III Made of: q.v.:(1) by tat. comp., a house of crystal: yatra sPawikaharmyam, Ki.;(2) -mayaH (yI, yaM), a vessel of clay: mfnmayaM pAtram, R.;(3) by deriv., surely my heart is of iron: nUnaM hfdayaM mamAyasam, Ram.IV In partitive sense:(1) by gen., by one of which: yezAmekatamena, P.;(2) by loc., of the kingdoms you have seen: Bavaddyzwezu rAzwrezu, D.; (3) gen. expr. by comp. when of follows a superlative, best of men: puruzottamaH (mA, maM), A.r.; greatest of all: sarvamahat (f. tI), S. k. Ph.: one of the wives (= one wife): ekA BAryA, J.; many of these: bahUnImAni, Mah. V. To denote cause: expr. by ins., of sorrow: Sokena, A. r.: v. From.VI To denote descent: expr. by deriv. or by comp., of the lunar race: somavaMSIyaH (yA, yaM), Mah.; prince of high blood: kulajaH kumAraH, N. Ph.: of late: aDunA; of old: purA.

OF , prep. expressed generally by the genitive case; as, ‘of me,’ mama; ‘of him,’ tasya; ‘of that man,’ tasya puruzasya. It is frequently expressed by the crude form of a noun in the first member of a compound; as, ‘best of all,’ sarvvaSrezWaH -zWA -zWaM; ‘lord of men,’ narapatiH m.; ‘made of wood,’ kAzWa- nirmmitaH -tA -taM. When it denotes ‘out of,’ ‘from amongst,’ it is expressed by maDyAt or maDye, affixed to the gen. c., or crude form; as, ‘of all men,’ sarvvapuruzamaDyAt or sarvvapuruzARAM maDyAt or maDye. It may sometimes be rendered by the abl. c., in phrases where ‘from’ may be substituted in English; as, ‘of a child, or from childhood,’ bAlyAt; ‘of a race of kings, or descended from a race of kings,’ rAja- kulAt prasUtaH or rAjakulaprasUtaH. It may even be rendered by the instr. c., in phrases where ‘by’ may be substituted in English; as, ‘hospitably entertained of the king,’ i. e. ‘by the king,’ rAjYA satkftaH. Where ‘of’ denotes ‘property,’ ‘possession,’ ‘connexion with,’ ‘belonging to,’ &c., it may either be expressed by the use of such words as sambanDI -nDinI &c., vizayaH -yA -yaM, vizayakaH &c., or by the gen. case, as in some of the foregoing examples. Very frequently an adjective compound involves some of these senses of the preposition; as, ‘a bird of a red color,’ raktavarRaH pakzI; ‘a man of great valor,’ mahAvIryyaH puruzaH; ‘a woman of great wealth,’ mahADanA strI. For the other senses of this preposition, see ‘by,’ ‘from,’ ‘out,’ ‘among.’ ‘Of late,’ arvAk, arvAkkAle, nUtanakAle; ‘of old,’ purA, purastAt, pUrvvaM, prAkkAle; ‘son of a grandson,’ prapOtraH; ‘pupil of a pupil,’ praSizyaH,

Gen. ex. by loc., aDi pr., upari (with gen.). 2 (Time, place) by loc.; ‘o(n) the shore’ tIre, tIropAMte, upatIraM. 3 (With verbs of motion) by loc. or instr., (skaMDena or skaMDe CAgaM gfhItvA); ‘go o(n) foot’ padByAM gam 1 P. 4 (Direction) by loc. or by tas, tra affixed; ‘o(n) the left’ vAmataH; ‘o(n) all sides’ sarvataH, sarvatra, samaMtataH. 5 (After) ex. by abl. or loc. abs.; ‘o(n) his arrival’ tasmin Agate, tadAgamanAt; or by gerund; ‘o(n) hearing his speech’ tasya vacaH SrutvA. 6 (Concerning) vizaya-saMbaMDin in comp. or by comp.; ‘a work o(n) morale’ nItigraMTaH; ‘so o(n)’ ityAdi (a.); ‘hence, o(n) thy life’ svajIvitaM yadi vAMCasi tarhi drAgapasara, apasarAsmAtsTAnAnno cet tvaM jIvitena viyokzyase; ‘o(n) o(n), to the combat’ nanu yudDAya prayAta. adv. agrataH, agre, pra pr.; ‘having clothes o(n)’ parihitavasra. [On]ward, a. agresara (rI f.), agragAmin; varDizRu. [On]wards, adv. agre, agrataH, purataH.

ON (prep.): I In contact with:(1) by loc., lying on a grass bed: saMvizwaH kuSaSayane, R.; putting on his head: SirasyAropya; Vi.; to fall on the ground: BUmO patati, Mr.;(2) upari (= over: q.v.): (with gen.), to throw on Vairodhaka: vEroDakasyopari nipAtanAya, Mu. N. B. The ins. must be used after verbs of motion: to go on horse: aSvena gacCati, S.; carrying on his shoulders: skanDenodUhya, D.; take me to (our) house on a fresh cloud: naya mAM navena vasatiM payomucA, V.II. = at, near:(1) by loc., a cow-station on the Ganges: gaNgAyAM GozaH, Kav.; on the north: uttarasyAM diSi, Ku.;(2) by affix tas, on the right: dakziRataH; on the left: vAmataH; on the rear: pfzWataH; on both sides: uBayataH.III At the time of: by loc., on the first of Āṣāḍha: AzAQasya praTamadivase, Me.; on the following day: parasminnahani (or commonly, paredyuH).IV = after: q.v.: by loc. abs., on her departure: gatAyAM tasyAm, K. V. Denoting logical basis of connexion: expr. by ins., on one condition: ekenABisanDinA, Sa.; on oath: SapaTena (?).VI Concerning: q.v.: expr. by comp., a treatise on spheres: golaprabanDaH, Go.VII To denote various rela- -tions: v. The several verbs after which it is used. Miscell.: on high: uccEH; on a sudden: sapadi; on the wing: v. To fly; on the alert: sAvaDAnaH (nA, naM); on hand: hastagataH (tA, taM); the gods were on (the side of) Arjuna: devA arjunato'Bavan, S. k.
ON (adv.): I After verbs: gen. not expr. II Attached to the body: aNge. Ph.: and so on: ityAdi (mfn.).

ON , prep. aDi, ni prefixed, upari affixed. — (Denoting contact with the upper part of a thing) expressed by the loc. c., or by upari affixed to the crude form or gen. c.; as, ‘on the table,’ Palake or Palakopari or Palakasyopari; rain falls on the ground, BUmO patati vfzwiH; ‘having placed the wood on his shoulder,’ kAzWaM skanDe kftvA; ‘placed on the fire,’ agnizWaH [Page551-a+ 51] -zWA -zWaM. The instr. c. is elegantly used for the loc. in similar phrases; as, ‘he carries the wood on his shoulder,’ kAzWaM skanDena vahati; ‘to go on foot,’ pAdAByAM gam; ‘conduct me home on a horse,’ aSvena mAM vasatiM naya. — (At, or near) expressed by loc. c., or by nikawe, samIpaM, upAnte &c. affixed, or by upa prefixed; as, ‘on the shore, tIre, tIranikawe, tIro- pAnte, upatIraM; ‘on the throat,’ upakaRWaM. — (At the time of) expressed by the loc. c., as, ‘on Monday,’ somavAre; ‘on their arrival,’ tezu Agatezu; ‘on the corn being cut,’ Sasye lUne sati, or even by the abl. c., as, ‘on seeing him,’ taddarSanAt, or by the indecl. part., as, ‘on seeing that,’ tad dfzwvA; ‘on hearing that,’ tacCrutvA. — (Toward or for) prati af- fixed, or expressed by gen. or loc. c; as, ‘have pity on me,’ mAM prati or mama or mayi dayAM kuru. — (Dependence on) ex- pressed by acc. c., after such verbs as avalamb, ASri &c.; as, ‘he relies on me,’ mAm avalambate. — (Concerning, relating to) vizayaH -yA -yaM, vizayakaH -kA -kaM, sambanDI -nDinI &c.; as, ‘a treatise on mathematics,’ gaRitavizayakaM SAstraM. — (Performing on an instrument) expressed by acc. c. after vad in caus.; as, ‘he plays on a lute,’ vIRAM vAdayati. The affixes tas, tra and dA, often express the sense of ‘on’; as, ‘on both sides,’ uBayatas, uBayatra, uBayapArSvatas; ‘on all sides,’ sarvvatas, samantatas, aBitas, samantAt, sarvvatra; ‘on the one hand,’ ekatas; ‘on all occasions,’ sarvvadA; ‘on one occasion,’ ekadA; ‘on another occasion,’ anyadA. The following are other ex- amples of instr., and other cases used adverbially to ex- press this prep.; ‘on the north-east of the city,’ prAguttareRa nagarAt; ‘on this account,’ anena hetunA; ‘on account of, or in consequence of anger,’ kopAt. See ACCOUNT; ‘on the other side,’ anyapArSvena, anyena pArSvena; ‘immediately on hear- ing this,’ tacCravaRamAtrAt; ‘on a sudden,’ akasmAt, sahasA; ‘on high,’ uccEs, uccakEs, uccaM, UrdDvaM, UrdDve; ‘set on foot,’ ArabDaH -bDA -bDaM, udyataH -tA -taM, pracalIkftaH &c.

ON , adv. (Forward, in progression) agre, agraM, agratas or ex- pressed by pra prefixed; as, ‘going on,’ agre gamanaM, pragamanaM. — (Continuance) expressed by the verb As in combination with the pres. or indecl. part. of another verb. See KEEP, CONTINUE. (Upon the body, as clothes, &c.). See To PUT ON.
ON DIT: (1) kila (enclitic); (2).. iti SrUyate; etc.
ON-DIT , adv. kiMvadantI, janapravAdaH, janavAdaH, lokapravAdaH.
ONCE: I One time:(1) sakft, even o.: sakfdapi, K.;(2) ekavAram, o. and again:(1) asakft; (2) vAraM vAram;(3) muhuH.II At one time: kadA- cit.III Formerly: q.v.: purA.

ONCE, AT: I. At the same time:(1) yugapat; (2) samakAlam;(3) ekAvasaram;(4) samam, Ki. Ph.: at o. perspicuous and deep: prasannagamBIraH (rA, raM), Ki.; at o. terrific and pleasant: BIma- kAntaH (ntA, ntaM), B.II. Immediately: q.v.: (1) sadyaH;(2) tatkzaRAt.

ONCE , adv. (One time) sakft, ekavAraM -re, ekakftvas, ekakAle, ekasamaye. — (On a certain time) ekadA, kadAcit. — (Formerly) pUrvvaM, purA. See the word. (At once, at the same time) samakAle, ekakAle, ekavAre, ekadA. — (All at once) yugapat, yOgapadyena, ekapadaM -de. — (All at once in a body) saNGaSas. — (All at once, suddenly) akasmAt. — (At once, immediately) sadyas, tatkAle, tatkzaRe. — (Once more) punarapi.
On-dit, s. kila ind.; See Rumour.

One, a. eka; ‘o(ne) of two’ ekatara; ‘o(ne) of many’ ekatama; ‘only o(ne)’ ananya; ‘fixed on o(ne) object’ ananyavizaya, ananyavftti. 2 (Any) kaScana, kopi. 3 (Same) eka, tad with eva; ‘at o(ne) time’ yugapat, samaM, ekakAle ‘having o(ne) meaning’ ekArTa. s. janaH, naraH, manuzyaH; gen. not ex.; ‘o(ne) should always protect oneself’ AtmAnaM satataM rakzet; ‘o(ne) by o(ne)’ ekEkaSaH, ekEkaM, pratyekaM, pfTakpfTak; ‘o(ne) day’ kadA-cit, kadApi kAle; ‘young or little o(ne)s’ SiSujanaH, bAlAH; ‘in o(ne) way’ ekaDA; ‘o(ne)-self’ Atman m., svayaM ind.; ‘o(ne)s own’ sva, nija, AtmIya, svIya, Atma in comp.; ‘to be at o(ne)’ saman 4 A; ‘o(ne)-eyed’ ekAkza, kARa, ekAkzihIna; ‘o(ne)-sided’ asama, ekpakzIyaekapakzIya, ekadeSIya; ‘o(ne) another’ anyonyaM, parasparaM, itaretaraM; ‘to be o(ne)self again’ prakftimApad 4 A, saMjYAM laB 1 A; See ‘come to senses’. under Sense; ‘to bring to o(ne)self’ prakftO sTA c. (sTApayati). [One]ness, s. ekatvaM, ekaBAvaH, advEtaM, aBedaH, aviSezaH. Once, adv. sakft, ekavAraM. 2 (‘O(nce) upon a time’) ekadA, aTEkadA, aTa kadAcit. 3 purA, pUrvaM, prAkkAle; ‘at o(nce)’ samaM, yugapat, ekakAle, samakAle-laM; sadyaH, sapadi, tatkza-RAt, tatkzaRena, tatkAle; ‘all at o(nce)’ aka-smAt, ekapade; ‘o(nce) more’ punarapi, BUyaH, punaH.

ONE: I In gen. sense:(1) ekaH (kA, kaM), not o. of you: Bavatsu nEkam, N. xiv. 44.; in o. hollow: ekasmin koware, K.; one-horse carriage: ekASvayAnam and sim. comp.s. (?);(2) ekEkaH (kA, kaM) (distributive), takes one Dinār every day: pratidinamekEkaM dInAraM gfhRAti, P.; gave o. code to each: ekEkAM saMhitAmEkakasmE dadO, B. p. One of two: ekataraH (rA, raM), one of many: eka- tamaH (mA, mat), even by o. of which: yezAmekatame- nApi, P. v. 3. One by one: ekEkaSaH, A. r. O. day: ekadA, K. At o. time: ekasmin samaye, L. II In contrast to other or another: ekaH (kA, kaM), the o. brought the kings under subjection, the other . eko nfpatIn vaSamanayat . apara ., R. viii. 19.; one is grinding paints, another stringing flowers: ekA varRakaM pinazwi . aparA sumanaso gumPati, Mr.; their clans are fourteen; one is derived from the mind of Brahmā, another from the Vedas, ano- ther from the fire: tAsAM caturdaSa kulAni . ekaM kamala- yonermanasaH samutpannam, anyadvedveByaH saMBUtam, anyadagne rudBUtam, K.; what will o. say of the other: kiM BaRati eka ekasya, Sa.; on the o. hand . on the other: ekatra . ekatra (better anyatra or aparatra), K.; on the o. hand . on the other: ekataH . anyataH, Vi. Ph.: at one time . at another time: kadAcit . kadAcit, R.III. Denoting identity: expr. by tad, but not the o.: na punaH saH, Mr.; I am the o.: so'hamasmi, D.: v. Same. Ph.: all the ethical systems are at one that innocence is a car- dinal virtue: DarmaSAstrARAmahiMsA paramo Darma ityatrEkamatyam, H.; the great-minded are one in mind, in word, in action: manasyekaM vacasyekaM karmaRyekaM mahAtmanAm, H. i. 100.IV In connexion with rel. pro.: expr. by tad, I do not see o. whom she has not embraced: na hi taM paSyAmi yo'nayA nopagUQaH, K. V. Equiv. to some o., any o.: kaScit: v. Any, some.VI In an indefinite sense (= men) janaH or lokaH, one would say: jano or loko vadi- zyati. Ph.: (a) little ones: SiSavaH: v. Child; (b) one-eyed: ekAkza (f. kzI) or gen. kARa (f. RA).

ONE , a. (Single in number) ekaH -kA -kaM; ‘one man,’ ekapuruzaH. — (Indefinitely) ‘some one,’ ‘any one,’ kaScit &c., kaScana &c., ko'pi &c. See SOME. (Mutuality) ‘one another,’ parasparaH -rA -raM, itaretaraH &c., anyonyaH -nyA -nyaM; ‘things that are equal to the same, are equal to one another,’ yAvantaH padArTAH [Page551-b+ 51] pratyekam ekena kenacit samAs te sarvve miTaH samAnAH; ‘one after ano- ther,’ anupUrvvaSas, kramaSas, krame krame. — (Same, like) ekaH -kA -kaM, samaH -mA -maM, tulyaH -lyA -lyaM; ‘at one time,’ ekakAle, ekapade; ‘of one color,’ ekavarRaH -rRA -rRaM, samavarRaH &c.; ‘having one object,’ ekArTaH -rTA -rTaM, ekAgraH -grA -graM; ‘having one occupation,’ ekavfttiH &c., ‘in one place,’ ekasTAne, ekatra; ‘collected,’ in one place,’ ekasTaH &c., ekOGaBUtaH -tA -taM. — (One only, but one) ananyaH -nyA -nyaM; ‘having one only refuge,’ ananyagatiH &c.; ‘having the mind fixed on one object,’ ananyamanaskaH &c., ananyaBAvaH &c. — (One by one) ekEkaM, ekEkaSas, ekaSas, pratyekaM, pfTak, pfTak pfTak. — (One day) ekadA, kadAcit; ‘in one way,’ ekaDA; ‘on the one hand,’ ekatas; ‘one of many,’ ekatamaH -mA -maM; ‘one of two,’ ekataraH -rA -raM; ‘one of these,’ tezAm ekaH, tatrEkaH; ‘one year old heifer,’ ekAbdA; ‘one year old calf,’ ekavatsaro vatsaH.

ONE , s. (Such a one, such and such a person) amukaH, amukajanaH. — (A man, a person) janaH, vyaktiH f., manuzyaH; ‘one's self,’ AtmA m. (n), svayaM indecl.; ‘by resemblance to one's self,’ AtmOpamyena; ‘done by one's self,’ svayaNkftaH -tA -taM; ‘one's own,’ sva, Atma in comp.; ‘like one's own body,’ svaSarIravat; AtmaSarIravat; ‘one's own house,’ AtmagfhaM, svagfhaM. See OWN.

ONE ANOTHER, ONE .THE OTHER: (1) anyonyaH (nyA, nyat), why do you eat o. a.'s flesh: kasmAdyU- yamanyonyaM mAMsaM BakzayaTa, Kar.; placing o. a.'s attributes on o. a.: anyonyasminnanyonyaDarmAnaDyasya, S.;(2) itaretaraH, (rA, rat) feeding o. a.: itaretaraM BojayataH, S. k.; without distinguishing one from the other: itaretarAvivekena, S.;(3) parasparaH, (rA, raM) all spoke to o. a.: UcuH sarve parasparam, A. r.; one with the other: paraspareRa, R. vii. 14.
ONE-EYED , a. ekAkzaH -kzA -kzaM, ekadfk m. f. n. (S), ekAkzivikalaH -lA -laM, ekanetraH -trA -traM, ekacakzUH -kzUH -kzuH (s), kARaH -RA -RaM, kAReyaH -yI -yaM, kAReraH -rI -raM.
ONE-HANDED , a. ekakaraH -rA -raM, ekahastaH -stA -staM, ekapARiH -RiH -Ri.
Oneirocritic, [Oneirocritic]al, a. svapnavicArin.
ONEIROCRITIC , ONEIROCRITICAL, a. svapnavicArI m. (n), svapnaprakASakaH, svapnArTajYApakaH, svapnArTaboDakaH.
Oneiromancy, s. svapnArTavicAraH, svapnArTajYApanaM.
ONEIROMANCY , s. svapnavicAraH, svapnaprakASanaM, svapnArTajYApanaM, svapnArTaboDanaM, svapnaparIkzA, svapnAdilakzaRAd BavizyatsUcanaM or SuBASuBakaTanaM.
ONENESS: ekatA, S. p. b.: v. Unity.
ONENESS , s. ekatA -tvaM, EkyaM, ekIBAvaH, EkyaBAvaH, advEtaM, aBedaH. — (Doctrine of oneness in theology). See UNITY.
To ONERATE , v. a. saBAraM -rAM kf, BAravantaM -vatIM -vat kf. See To LOAD.
Onerous, a. durBara, guru, guruBAra, durvaha, duHsaha.
ONEROUS: (1) gurU (f. rvI) (= heavy);(2) durBaraH (rA, raM) (= oppressive).
ONEROUS , a. durBaraH -rA -raM, duHsahaH -hA -haM, durvahaH -hA -haM, BArI -riRI -ri (n), BAravAn -vatI -vat (t), saBAraH -rA -raM, kazwakaraH -rA -raM, pIqAkaraH &c., guruH -ruH -ru.
ONESIDED: asamaH (mA, maM) (= inequal): v. Partial.
ONESIDEDNESS: asamatA (= inequality): v. Partiality.
Onion, s. palAMquH, sukaMdakaH.
ONION: (1) palARquH;(2) sukandaH.
ONION , s. palARquH m., sukandakaH, mukandakaH, mukundakaH, durdrumaH, dudrumaH, latArkaH, gfYjanaH, muKaganDakaH, muKadUzaRaH, tIkzRakandaH, mahAkandaH, nIcaBojyaH.

Only, a. eka, eva, ekAkin, kevala, mAtra-mAtraka in comp., advitIya, ananya; ‘having that as the o(nly) recourse’ tadEkaSaraRa, ananyagatika. adv. kevalaM, eva, mAtra in comp.; ‘not o(nly) but’ na kevalaM followed by api or kiMtu.

ONLY (adj.): (1) eka eva (ekEva, ekameva), I was the o. daughter born of them: tayorahamekEvAtmajA samutpannA, K.;(2) eka- in comp., (my) old infirm mother who has an o. son in me: madekaputrA jananI jarAturA, N.;(3) by adv.: q.v.

ONLY (adv.): (1) kevalam, (best equiv.), killing me is not o. killing an animal: na kevalaM prARivaDo vaDo mama, N.; (but) o. (he) does not bear trans- gression: kevalaM na sahate vilaNGanam, Ki.;(2) by mAtra in comp., black o. in colour: varRamAtreRa kfzRaH, Me.;(3) with eva giving emphasis, there is o. one means: eka evopAyo'sti, K. s.

ONLY , a. (Single, one alone) ekaH -kA -kaM, kevalaH -lA -lI -laM, kevalI -linI -li (n), kEvalyaH -lyA -lyaM, mAtraH in comp. mAtrakaH -kA -kaM, advitIyaH -yA -yaM; ‘an only son,’ ekaputraH, ekasUnuH m. — (This and no other) ananyaH -nyA -nyaM, nAnyaH -nyA -nyat; ‘having one only refuge,’ ananyagatiH -tiH -ti; ‘his only business is reading the Vedas,’ vedADyayanAt tasya kAryyaM nAnyat.
ONLY , adv. kevalaM, mAtraM -treRa -trAt, kuwwAraM, ekAntatas, eva; ‘by calculation only,’ gaRitamAtreRa, kevalagaRitena, gaRitenEva; ‘touch only,’ sparSamAtraM; ‘from touch only,’ sparSamAtrAt.
ONOMANCY , s. nAmAkzaralakzaRAd BavizyatsUcanaM or SuBASuBakaTanaM.
ONOMATOP ŒIA, s. (In rhetoric) anukaraRaM, anukaraRaSabdaH, SabdAnukaraRaM.
Onomatopœia, s. anukAraH; anukaraRaM.
ONOMATOPŒIA: avyaktAnukaraRam, S. k.
Onset, s. A-aBi-kramaH-maRaM, avaskaMdaH, aBi-saMpAtaH, ApAtaH, aBigrahaH, aByAGAtaH.
ONSET: avaskandaH: v. Attack.
ONSET , s. AkramaH -maRaM, aBikramaH -maRaM, aDikramaH -maRaM, aBiyogaH, aBigrahaH, avaskandaH -ndanaM, aByAGAtaH; ‘emulative onset,’ ahampUrvikA.
Onslaught, s. aByAGAtaH; See Onset.
ONSLAUGHT: aBiGAtaH: v. Also invective.
ONTOLOGIST , s. sattvavidyAjYaH, sattvamAtravicArI m. (n), BUtamAtravicArI m.
Ontology, s. sattvavidyA, BUtavicAraH. [Ontolog]ist, s. sattvavidyAjYaH.
ONTOLOGY: *sattvavijYAnam; sattvavicAraH; and sim. comps.
ONTOLOGY , s. sattvavidyA, sattvamAtravicAraH, BUtamAtravicAraH.
ONWARD (adj.): (1) agresaraH (rI, raM);(2) varDizRu (mfn.) (= increasing).
ONWARD,-s (adv.): (1) agre;(2) agrataH;(3) purataH.

ONWARD , ONWARDS, adv. agre, agratas, puras, puratas, purastAt, aBitas, aBimuKaM -Ke, pratimuKaM -Ke, agraBAgaM, prati, uttareRa, UrdDvaM, or expressed by pra; as, ‘proceeding onwards,’ agre gamanaM, agragamanaM, pragamanaM, prasTAnaM. — (A little further) kiYcidantaraM -reRa, kiYcidaparatas.

ONWARD , a. (Advanced, in advance) agraH -grA -graM, agrimaH -mA -maM, agragAmI -minI -mi (n), agragaH -gA -gaM, agrataHsaraH -rA -raM, agrasaraH -rA -raM, pragataH -tA -taM. — (Increased) varDitaH -tA -taM, pravfdDaH -dDA -dDaM, prarUQaH -QA -QaM.
ONYX: gomedaBedaH; pItaratnam (?), Bha.
ONYX , s. (Precious stone) gomedakaH -kaM, SivaDAtuH m.

Ooze, v. i. (SanEH) sru-kzar-gal- 1 P, syaMd 1 A, pra-snu 2 P, rI 4 A. v. t. sru c., syaMd c., &c. s. kzaratpaMkaH, mfdumfttikA. 2 sravaH, dravaH, DArA. [Ooz]ing, s. syaMdanaM, kzaraRaM, sravaH. [Ooz]y, a. sadrava.
OOZE (v. i.): (1) sravati, pari-, (sru, c. 1.). and the secret will o. out: rahasyaYca sravati, D. ii.; (2) kzarati (kzar, c. 1.);(3) rIyate (rI, c. 4.) (rare).
OOZE (subs.): kzaritam: v. Also flow.

To OOZE , v. n. SanEH SanEH sru (c. 1. sravati, srotuM) or syand (c. 1. syandate -ndituM) or prasyand or kzar (c. 1. kzarati -rituM) or rI (c. 4. rIyate, retuM) or gal (c. 1. galati -lituM), krame krame or vindukrameRa kzaraRaM kf.
OOZE , s. (Moist mud) sadravapaNkaH, cikkaRapaNkaH, kzaratpaNkaH. — (Exuda- tion) syandanaM, sravaH, vindusrAvaH, syannarasaH, svedaH, dravaH, DArA.
OOZING , s. SanEH SanEH sravaRaM or syandanaM or kzaraRaM or galanaM.
OOZING , part. SanEH SanEH syandI -ndinI -ndi (n) or syandamAnaH -nA -naM or nisyandamAnaH -nA -naM or syannaH -nnA -nnaM or kzaran -rantI -rat (t) or sravan &c. or rIRaH -RA -RaM.
OOZY (adj.): sarasaH (sA, saM): v. Moist, wet.
OOZY , a. sadravapaNkamayaH -yI -yaM, kzaratpaNkamayaH &c., sadravaH -vA -vaM.
OPACITY: kaluzatA or kAluzyam: v. Transparency.

OPACITY , OPAQUENESS, s. (The quality of being impervious to light) prakASABedyatA, praBABedyatA, kiraRABedyatA, asvacCatA, prakASapra- tibanDakatvaM, prakASaroDakatvaM, dfzwiroDakatA. — (Obscurity) nizpraBatA, aprakASatA, kaluzatvaM, praBAhInatA, sAnDakAratA, aprasannatA. — (Disease in the eyes) SuklaM.
Opal, s. pulakaH, vimalakaH.
OPAL: perh. pulakaH or vimalakaH, V. m. 80. 4.
OPAL , s. SivaDAtuH m., pARqumfttikA, vajrABaH, kzIraspawikaH, gomedasanniBaH.
Opaque, a. prakASABedya, kiraRABedya; asvacCa, kaluza, nizpraBa, sAMDakAra. [Opaque]ness, Opacity, s. asvacCatA, nizpraBatA, kAluzyaM. 2 SuklaM.

OPINIATIVENESS , s. svamatABimAnaM -nitA, svamatAgrahaH, matABimAnaM, durAgrahaH, svamatajAqyaM.

OPINION: I In gen.: matam, in my o. the Vaiśe- ṣika doctrine is good: vESezikaM cArU mataM mataM me, N. xxii. 36.II Estimation: expr. with mataH (tA, taM), aBi-, win good o. of your husband: BatarbahumatA Bava, Sa. iv.III Honour, fame: q.v.: mAnaH.

OPINION , s. mataM, matiH f., budDiH f., sammataM, tarkaH, vicAraH, anumAnaM, boDaH, BAsaH, CandaH; ‘a different opinion,’ vikalpaH, paramataM; ‘difference of opinion,’ matiBedaH, mataBedaH, vipratipattiH f.; ‘op- posed in opinion,’ vipratipannaH -nnA -nnaM; ‘public opinion,’ lokamataM, janamataM; ‘regard for it,’ lokalajjA, janalajjA; ‘atheistical opinion,’ nAstikamataM; ‘legal opinion,’ sUtraM. — (Estimation) mAnaM, sammAnaM.
OPINIONATE, -D: svamatabadDa (f. dDA) and sim. comp.s. (?).
Opium, s. ahiPenaM, aPenaM.
OPIUM: (1) ahiPenam:(2) APUkam, “APUkaM SozaRaM grAhi”, Bha.
OPIUM , s. aPenaM, ahiPenaM, KasKasarasaH, upavizaM.
OPOSSUM: *OpasamaH; SAvakakozaBfjjantuviSezaH.
OPPIDAN , a. nAgarikaH -kI -kaM, nAgaraH -rI -raM, pOraH -rI -raM.
OPPILATED , p. p. sambADaH -DA -DaM, saNkIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, saNkulaH -lA -laM.
Opponent, a. virudDa, pratikUla, vi-prati-pakza, vErin. s. SatruH, ariH, vErin, vi-prati-pakzaH; pratiyodDf, pratiyogin, pratiroDakaH all m.
OPPONENT: pratidvandvin (mfn.): v. Also adver- -sary, enemy.

OPPONENT , a. viroDI -DinI -Di (n), pratiroDI &c., virudDaH -dDA -dDaM, vErI -riRI &c., pratiyogI &c., pratikUlaH -lA -laM, vipakzaH -kzA -kzaM, pratipakzaH &c., viparItaH -tA -taM, vimuKaH -KA -KaM, parANmuKaH &c., vimataH -tA -taM, pratIpakaH &c.

OPPONENT , s. pratiroDI m. (n), viroDI m., vErI m., SatruH m., ariH m., pratiyogI m., pratirodDA m. (dDf), pratiroDakaH, pratibanDakaH, pratiyodDA m. (dDf), pratipakzaH, aBiyAtI m. (n), vijigIzuH m. — (In controversy) vivAdI m. (n), pUrvvavAdI m., agravAdI m., prativAdI m., uttaravAdI m., pUrvvapakzI m., pratipakzI m., vAdI m.

Opportune, a. samayocita, prAptakAla, kAla-yogya, prastAvasadfSa (SI f.), prAptAvasara, sAmayika-prAstAvika- (kI f.). [Opportune]ly, adv. prAptakAlaM, kAle, sTAne, yaTAsamayaM, yaTAvasaraM, prastAvasadfSaM, kAlocitaM. [Opportune]ness, s. kA-lOcityaM, prastAvayogyatA. Opportunity, s. prastAvaH, avakASaH, avasaraH, kAlaH, samayaH, prasaMgaH, velA, kAryakAlaH, yogaH. 2 sADanaM, upAyaH, prayukti f.; ‘lose an o(pportunity)’ kAlaM kzip 6 P or hf 1 P; ‘seizing an (pportunity)’ avasaraM gfhItvA, gfhItAvasara, labDAvakASa; ‘to await an (pportunity)’ avasaraM pratipA c. (pA-layati).
OPPORTUNE: I Timely:(1) samayocitaH (tA, taM);(2) prAptakAlaH (lA, laM); and sim. comp.s. II Fig., becoming: q.v.

OPPORTUNE , a. samayopayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, sanagrocitaH -tA -taM, samayAnukUlaH -lA -laM, sAmayikaH -kI -kaM, kAlikaH &c., kAlasadfSaH -SI -SaM, kAlayogyaH -gyA -gyaM, prastAvasadfSaH &c., prAstAvikaH -kI -kaM, prAptA- vasaraH -rA -raM, prAptakAlaH -lA -laM, prAptasamayaH -yA -yaM, prasaNgopayuktaH &c., kAkatAlIyaH -yA -yaM.
OPPORTUNELY: (1) yaTAvasaram;(2) yaTAsamayam; (3) kAle: v. Time.
OPPORTUNELY , adv. yaTAvasaraM, kAle, sTAne, samayAnusAreRa, samayopayuktaM, prasaNgAnusArAt, prastAvasadfSaM, yaTAvakASaM, yaTAsamayaM, yaTAprasaNgaM, kAla- yogyaM, yaTAyogyaM, velAyAM.
OPPORTUNENESS: (1) Ocityam (= fitness);(2) prAptakAlatA (of time).
OPPORTUNENESS , s. samayopayuktatA, kAlayogyatA, samayOcityaM, prasaNgayo- gyatA, prasaNgAnukUlyaM, kAlikatvaM.

OPPORTUNITY: avasaraH, kings are to be approa- ched (when) o. ies. (occur): avasaropasarpaRIyA rAjAnaH, Sa. v.; to give an o.: avasarapradAnAya, Sr.; this is the o. to show myself: avasaro'yamAtmAnaM darSayitum, Sa.: looking up for an o. for (discharging) an arrow: bARAvasaraM pratIkzya, Ku. iii. 64.: v. Also time.

OPPORTUNITY , s. avasaraH, prasaNgaH, samayaH, prastAvaH, avakASaH, kAlaH, kAryyakAlaH, kAlayogaH, sanDiH m., kAlasanDiH m., velA, yogaH, suyogaH, sTAnaM, vAraH, prakramaH; ‘according to opportunity,’ yaTAvasaraM, yaTAprasaNgaM, yaTAvakASaM; ‘to lose one's opportunity,’ kAlaM hf (c. 1. harati, harttuM) or hA (c. 3. jahAti, hAtuM); ‘to await it,’ avasaraM pratipAl (c. 10. -pAlayati -yituM); ‘one who has found an opportunity,’ labDAvakASaH -SA -SaM. — (Means) sADanaM, upAyaH, sanDAnaM.

Oppose, v. t. vi-ni-prati-ruD 7 U, pratibaMD 9 P, pratikf 8 U, pratikUlayati (D.), pratyavasTA 1 A, vi-prati-han 2 P, bAD 1 A, nivf c.; (in fighting) pratiyuD c.; saM-muKI-aBimuKI-kf 8 U or BU. [Oppos]ed, a. virudDa, viparIta, pratikUla, vipratipanna, bADita, vArita, asaMmata, vidvizwa; ‘o(pposed) to the practice of the world’ lokAcAravirudDa, lokAsaMmata, lokavidvizwa. 2 itara in comp.; ‘o(pposed) to false’ miTyetara. [Oppos]er, s. viroDakaH, pratihaMtf m. Opposite, a. saM-prati-aBimuKa (KI f.), saMmuKasTa. 2 virudDa, viroDin, viparIta, patikUla, vi-prati-pakza, pratidvaMdvin, viparyasta, vyatyasta, itara in comp. ‘o(pposite) of natural’ sahajetara; savyetara, &c. 3 para, apara, aMtara in comp.; ‘the o(pposite) bank’ pAraM, tIrAMtaraM, aparatIraM. s. viparyayaH, vyatyAsaH, viparItaM; by (a.). [Opposit]ion, s. vEpa-rityaM, prAtikUlyaM, viroDaH, vipakzatA, viparya-(ryA)yaH, vyatyayaH, vyatyAsaH, viparyAsaH. 2 viroDaH, pratikriyA, pratibaMDaH, pratiyogaH-yatnaH, vyAGAtaH, bADaH-DA. 3 viroDakajanAH, pratiyogipakzaH, viroDijanavargaH. 4 virudDa-dveza-BAvaH, vEraM. [Opposite]ly, adv. saM-aBi-muKaM, viparItaM, pratikUlaM, viparyayeRa.

OPPOSE (v. t.): I Lit.:(1) saMmuKayati;(2) saMmuKI- karoti.II In gen.:(1) nirURadDi (rUD, c. 7.) (= to check), to o. his progress: tatprasaraM nirodDum, Vi. iv. 6.;(2) pratikUlayati (nomi.) (= to act adversely), and it (passion) cannot be o.d by any one: na cAyaM kenApi pratikUlayituM Sakyate, K.;(3) pratikzipati (kzip, c. 6.) (= to refute: as of opinion), D. s.; pratiyoDayati (c. of yuD) (in fighting), D.;(4) nivArayati (vf, c. 10 (= to prevent).
OPPOSE (v. i.): in controversies: pratyavatizWate (sTA, c. 1.), others o. to this: atrApare pratyava- tizWante, S.

To OPPOSE , v. a. and n. (Act against, resist) pratikf, vipratikf, viprakf, pratiruD (c. 7. -ruRadDi -rodvuM), viruD, saMruD, virudDIBU, pratikUla (nom. pratikUlayati -yituM), pratikUlIBU, paryavasTA (c. 1. -tizWati -sTAtuM), [Page554-a+ 51] pratisamAs (c. 2. -Aste -AsituM), pratIpa (nom. pratIpAyate), pratihan (c. 2. -hanti -ntuM), viparItaH -tA -taM BU or as. — (Put in opposi- tion, set one against the other) virudDaM -dDAM kf, virudDIkf, parasparaM viruD, pratikUlIkf, viroDinaM -nIM kf. — (Hinder) nivf (c. 10. -vArayati -yituM), viGna (nom. viGnayati -yituM), bAD (c. 1. bADate -DituM), pratibanD (c. 9. -baDnAti -bandDuM), vihan, pratihan, vyAhan, ruD. — (Check) nigrah (c. 9. -gfhlAti -grahItuM).
OPPOSED: (1) virUdDa (f. dDA) (o. to practices, moral, etc.), M. viii. 46.; Ki. xiv. 25.; (2) pratikUlaH (lA, laM) (= adverse).

OPPOSED , p. p. virudDaH -dDA -dDaM, pratirudDaH &c., paryyavasTitaH -tA -taM, viparItaH -tA -taM, pratikUlaH -lA -laM, prAtikUlikaH -kI -kaM, viroDI -DinI -Di (n), vipratikftaH -tA -taM, viprakftaH &c., vipratipannaH -nnA -nnaM, pratiyAtaH -tA -taM. — (Hindered, checked) vAritaH -tA -taM, nivA- ritaH -tA -taM, bADitaH -tA -taM, vihataH &c., pratihataH &c., rudDaH &c., viGnitaH &c.; when ‘opposed’ signifies ‘the opposite of,’ itara may be used; as, ‘opposed to movable,’ jaNgametaraH -rA -raM.
OPPOSER , s. viroDI m. (n), pratiroDI m., paryavasTAtA m. (tf), prati- yogI m. (n), viroDakaH, prAtikUlikaH, pratihantakaH. See OPPONENT.

OPPOSITE (adj.): I Facing:(1) saMmuKa (f. KA);(2) saMmuKInaH (nA, naM).II Adverse, [Page490] contrary: q.v.:(1) virUdDa (f. dDA), of o. natures like darkness and light: tamaHprakASavadvirUdDa- svaBAvayoH, S.;(2) viroDin (f. nI), of o. views: viroDivacas (mfn.), Si. ii. 25.
OPPOSITE (subs.): I An enemy: q. v.: viro- Din (f. nI).II A contrary: q.v.: viparItam.

OPPOSITE , a. (Situated in front, facing) aBimuKaH -KA -KI -KaM, aBimuKagataH -tA -taM, aBimuKasTaH -sTA -sTaM, sammuKaH -KA -KaM, sammuKasTaH -sTA -sTaM, aBisammuKaH -KA -KaM, sammuKInaH -nA -naM, pratimuKaH -KA -KaM. — (Adverse, contrary) viparItaH -tA -taM, pratikUlaH -lA -laM, virudDaH -dDA -dDaM, viroDI -DinI -Di (n), pratiroDI &c., viparyyastaH -stA -staM, apasavyaH -vyA -vyaM, prasavyaH &c., apasavyakaH &c., pratipakzaH -kzA -kzaM, vipakzaH &c., avakawaH -wA -waM. — (Further, on the other side) paraH -rA -raM, aparaH -rA -raM; ‘the opposite bank,’ pAraM, paratIraM, tIrAntaraM. — (Reverse of) vyatyastaH -stA -staM, itara in comp.; as, ‘the opposite of movable,’ jaNgametaraH -rA -raM; ‘of white,’ sitetaraH &c.; ‘of left,’ vAmetaraH &c.; ‘of innate,’ sahajetaraH &c. — (Opposite side of the argument) uttarapakzaH, parapakzaH, pratipakzaH.
OPPOSITE , s. viparyyayaH, viparyyAyaH, vyatyayaH, vyatyAsaH, viparyyAsaH, viparItaM.
OPPOSITELY , adv. (In front) aBimuKaM, sammuKaM, pratimuKaM, sammuKInaM. — (Adversely) viparItaM, vEparItyena, pratikUlaM, virudDaM, viroDena, vipa- ryyayeRa, prAtikUlyena.

OPPOSITION: I The act:(1) viroDaH, -nam, etc.; (2) better by verb: v. To oppose.II Obstacle: q.v.: bADA. Ph.: without o.: aviroDena.III Contrariety, repugnance: q.v.: viroDaH. Ph.: in o. to: virUdDam: v. Aga- -inst.IV Adverse party: virUdDapakzaH (?).

OPPOSITION , s. viroDaH -DanaM, pratiroDaH -DanaM, pratikAraH, vipratikAraH, pratikriyA, pratyavasTAnaM, paryyavasTA -sTAnaM, pratiyogaH -gitA, vipratipattiH f., pratibanDakatA, pratibanDitA, pratiyatnaH. — (State of being opposed) virudDatA, viparItatA, vEparItyaM, pratikUlatA, pratipakzatA, prAtikUlyaM. — (Contrariety) viparyyayaH, viparyyAyaH, paryyayaH, viparyyAsaH, vEparItyaM, vyatyayaH, vyatyAsaH, nikAraH. — (Impediment) vyAGAtaH, viGnaH, vADaH -DA, pratibanDaH, avaroDaH, uparoDaH, niroDaH, roDaH. — (Collective body of opposers) viroDijanasamUhaH, pratiyogipakzaH, viroDakapakzaH. — (Hostile feeling) virudDaBAvaH, dvepaBAvaH; ‘opposition of interests,’ vipratipattiH f.; ‘in opposition to what was before said,’ pUrvvoktapratipakze.

Oppress, v. t. pIq 10, ard 1 P or c., upadru 1 P, bAD 1 A, ni-apa-kf 8 U, vipra-kf, upaplu 1 A, upa mfd 9 P or c., kfz c., aBidruh 4 P, aBiBU 1 P. [Oppress]ion, s. pIqA, pIqanaM, bADaH-DA, ardanaM, upamardaH, upaplavaH, upadravaH, ni-vipra-apa-kAraH, nEzWuryaM, krOryaM. [Oppress]ive, a. bADaka, pIqAkara (rI f.), upa-plavin, upadravin, pIqAprada, apakAraka; nizWura, atikrUra, kleSada. 2 atiBAravat. [Oppress]or, s. prajApIqakaH, upaplAvakaH, upadravin m., atyAcAraH, nizWuraH, krUracaritaH.

OPPRESS: (1) pIqayati, pra-, ut-, ni-, saM-, upa- (pIq, c. 10.), unjustly o. es men: anyAyataH pIqayati mAnavAn, Ram. i. 14. 17.; was o. ed with the enjoined price of (this) daughter: pIqito duhitf- SulkasaMsTayA, R. xi. 38.;(2) bADate or bADayati, pra-, pari-, (bAD, c.I and c. 10.), he o. es the three worlds: sa bADayati lokAMstrIn, Ram.;(3) upaplavate (pla, c. 1 (rare), Si.

To OPPRESS , v. a. pIq (c. 10. pIqayati -yituM), aBipIq, upapIq, nipIq, upanipIq, bAD (c. 1. bADate -DituM), prabAD, paribAD, aDibAD, druh (c. 4. druhyati, drohituM, drogDuM), aBidruh, kfz (c. 10. karzayati -yituM), aBidrohaM kf, ard (c. 10. ardayati -yituM), viqamb (c. 10. -qamba- yati -yituM), apakf, apakAraM kf, mardanaM kf, upamardanaM kf, praDfz (c. 10. -Darzayati -yituM), upadravaM kf, upaplavaM kf, nEzWuryyaM kf, krOryyaM kf, krUravat kf, aBiBU, balAtkAraM kf.
OPPRESSED , p. p. pIqitaH -tA -taM, bADitaH -tA -taM, atidrugDaH -gDA -gDaM, aBidruhyamARaH -RA -RaM, upadrutaH -tA -taM, viqambitaH -tA -taM, aBiBUtaH -tA -taM, apakftaH -tA -taM, AkulitaH -tA -taM.
OPPRESSION: I The act or that which op- -presses:(1) pIqanam, ut-, pra-, o. of people: prajApIqanam;(2) upadravaH;(3) upaplavaH (rare). II Misery: q.v.: pIqA.III A sense of weight: BAraH.

OPPRESSION , s. (The act) pIqanaM, prajApIqanaM, aBidrohaH, drohaH -haRaM, upadravaH, upadravakaraRaM, upamardaH -rdanaM, vimardaH -rdanaM, bADaH -DanaM, karzaRaM, pariplavaH, upaplavaH, upaplavakaraRaM, apakAraH, apakarmma n. (n), apakriyA, balAtkAraH, nizWuratA, nEzWuryyaM, krUratA, krOryyaM, dOrAtmyaM, utpAtaH, viqambanaM -nA, haWaH, anyAyakaraRaM. — (State) pIqA, bADA, pIqitatvaM. — (Weight) BAraH.
OPPRESSIVE: I Tyrannical:(1) pIqaka (f. qikA), ut-, pra-;(2) bADaka (f. DikA);(3) dArURa (f. RA) (= fierce).II Heavy, over- -powering: durBaraH (rA, raM).

OPPRESSIVE , a. (Cruelly severe, or tyrannical) bADakaH -kA -kaM, pIqAkaraH -rA -raM, pIqakaH -kA -kaM, upadravakArI -riRI -ri (n), upadravI &c., upamardakaH -kA -kaM, apakArakaH &c., sabADaH -DA -DaM, nizWuraH -rA -raM, krUraH -rA -raM, nirdayaH -yA -yaM, durvfttaH -ttA -ttaM, kleSadAyakaH -kA -kaM, kleSadaH -dA -daM, anyAyakArI &c. — (Heavy) BArI -riRI &c.
OPPRESSIVENESS: (1) pIqakatA etc. (?);(2) better by adj.
OPPRESSIVENESS , s. bADakatvaM -tA, sabADatA, kleSakatA, nEzWuryyaM, krOryyaM.
OPPRESSOR: (1) prajApIqakaH;(2) lokabADakaH; etc.: v. To oppress.
OPPRESSOR , s. prajApIqakaH, upadravakarttA m. (rttf), upadravI m. (n), krUra- caritaH, nizWuraH, nirdayaH, atyAcAraH, durAtmA m. (n), durjanaH, durvfttaH, dasyuH m.
OPPROBRIOUS: kutsitaH (tA, taM): v. Also dis- -graceful, blameable.

OPPROBRIOUS , a. nindakaH -kA -kaM, nindArTakaH &c., nindArUpaH -pA -paM, nindAtmakaH &c., garhAtmakaH &c., garhArTakaH &c., apavAdakaH &c., muKaraH -rA -raM, durmuKaH -KA -KaM, paruzaH -zA -zaM, garhyaH -rhyA -rhyaM.
OPPROBRIOUSLY: kftsitam: v. Also disgrace- -fully.
