OPPROBRIOUSNESS , s. nindakatvaM, apavAdakatA, aBivAdaH, pOruzyaM, mOKaryyaM.

Opprobrium, s. niMdA, garhA, kutsA, tira-skAraH, apavAdaH, avajYA, pariBavaH, vAcyatA, DikkAraH. Opprobrious, a. garhya, niMdA-tmaka, garhArUpa, niMdA-garhA-arTaka; paruza, muKara, dvezya. [Opprobrious]ly, adv. sApavAdaM, satira-skAraM. [Opprobrious]ness, s. garhyatA, niMdakatvaM.
OPPROBRIUM: kftsA: v. Reproach, blame.
OPPROBRIUM , s. nindA, apavAdaH, GfRA, garhA -rhaRaM, kutsA, tiraskAraH, avajYA -jYAnaM, pariBavaH, apamAnaM, vAcyatA, vacanIyatA, DikkriyA, kuKyAtiH f.
To OPPUGN , v. a. pratikf, vipratikf, pratiruD, viruD &c. See To OPPOSE.
OPPUGNANCY , s. viroDaH, pratiroDaH, prAtikUlyaM, vEparItyaM, pratiyogitA.
Optative, a. icCArTaka.
OPTATIVE: o. mood: ASaMsAvAcinI kriyA (after S. k.).
OPTATIVE , a. icCAsUcakaH -kA -kaM, icCAboDakaH &c., aBilAzaboDakaH &c., aBilAzajYApakaH &c. The grammatical symbol is sanantaH.
Optic, [Optic]al, a. cAkzuza (zI f.), cakzuH-netra in comp. 2 dfkSAstrasaMbaMDin. s. cakzuriMdriyaM, dfgiMdriyaM. Optics, s. dfgvidyA-SAstraM.
OPTIC, -AL: by comp., o. angle: *dykkoRaH; o. nerve: AlokavAhinI SirA (after SabdavAhinI, Sr.)
OPTIC , OPTICAL, a. (Pertaining to vision) cAkzuzaH -zI -zaM, dfzwi- vizayakaH -kA -kaM, dfzwisambanDI -nDinI &c. — (Pertaining to optics) dfkSAstrasambanDI &c., dfkSAstravizayakaH &c.
OPTIC , s. (Organ of sight) dfgindriyaM, cakzurindriyaM, darSanasADanaM.
OPTICIAN: *AlokayantrikaH and sim. comp.s.

OPTICIAN , s. (Maker of optic instruments) cAkzuzayantrakArakaH -karttA m. (rttf), dfzwisADakayantrakAraH, dfzwiyantravikretA m. (tf), cAkzuza- yantravikrayI m. — (Skilled in optics) dfkSAstrajYaH, cAkzuzajYAnI m. (n).
OPTICS: tejovijYAnam; prakASavijYAnam; AlokavijYAnam.
OPTICS , s. pl. dfgvidyA, cAkzuzavidyA, dfzwividyA, dfkSAstraM, dfzwivizayA vidyA, cAkzuzaM jYAnaM, darSAnuSAsanaM.
Optimacy, s. kulInavargaH-janAH.
OPTIMACY , s. kulInavargaH, kulInalokaH, kOlInyaM, kulInatA -tvaM.
Optimism, s. uttamatA, utkfzwatA.
OPTIMISM , s. uttamatA -tvaM, atyuttamatA -tvaM, sattamatA -tvaM.

Option, s. aBi-, ruci f., icCA, kAmaH, aBilAzaH, IpsitaM; vikalpaH, viBAzA (in grammar); ‘it is left to your o(ption)’ atra svarucyA vartatAM BavAn, yaTABilAzaM kriyatAM. [Option]al, a. vEkalpika-EcCika- (kI f.), kAmya, savikalpa, yaTAkAma, rucyaDIna, svecCAtaMtra. [Option]ally, adv. vikalpena, anya-tarasyAM, (hfkroranyatarasyAM), vA, viBAzayA.
OPTION: aBiruciH (?), is there any o. in the matter: kimatra kasyacit svaruciH, Vi. iv.: v. Choice.
OPTION , s. (Power of choosing) vikalpaH -lpakaH, anukalpaH, kalpaH, viBAzA, icCA, varaRADikAraH. — (Wish) icCA, aBilAzaH, kAmaH, manaskAmaH, ruciH f., aBiruciH, IpsitaM, aBIpsitaM.

OPTIONAL , a. vEkalpikaH -kI -kaM, vikalpakaH &c., savikalpakaH -kA -kaM, AnukalpikaH -kI -kaM, vikalpitaH -tA -taM, savikalpaH -lpA -lpaM, EcCikaH -kI -kaM, kAmyaH -myA -myaM, aBikAmikaH &c., yaTAkAmaH -mA -maM, viBA- zitaH -tA -taM; ‘an optional matter,’ vikalpavizayaH, viBAzAvizayaH.
OPTIONALLY , adv. savikalpaM -lpakaM, sAnukalpaM, vikalpena, vikalpapUrvvaM.
OPULENCE: (1) sam-fdDiH;(2) ESvaryam;(3) viBavaH.
OPULENCE , s. DanAQyatA, DanabAhulyaM, DanasampattiH f., sampattiH f., DanESvaryyaM, ESvaryyaM, mahADanatvaM, DanasamfdDiH f., lakzmIH f., SrIH f., lakzmIvattvaM.
Opulent, a. SrImat, Danin, DanAQya, vittavat, Dana-vitta-saMpanna, Danika, samfdDa, saMpanna, DaneSvara, bahuDana. Opulence, s. viBavaH, ESvaryaM, samfdDi f.
OPULENT: (1) samfdDiSAlin (f. nI): v. Rich.

OPULENT , a. SrImAn -matI -mat (t), DanAQyaH -QyA -QyaM, mahADanaH -nA -naM, bahuDanaH -nA -naM, atiDanI -ninI -ni (n), DanI &c., atiDa- navAn &c., DanavAn &c., bahuvittavAn &c., bahudravyavAn &c., vasumAn &c., arTavAn &c., sampattimAn &c., lakzmIvAn &c., samfdDaH -dDA -dDaM, sampannaH -nnA -nnaM, DaneSvaraH, lakzmISaH, surAH m. f. (rE), AQyaH &c., varDizRuH -zRuH -zRu, iByaH -ByA -ByaM.
OPULENTLY , adv. DanabAhulyena, DanAQyavat, mahADanavat, sampattipUrvvaM.

sanskrit.slp1: svapno nu mAyA nu matiBramo nu
sanskrit.word: स्वप्नो नु माया नु मतिभ्रमो नु
sanskrit.iast: svapno nu māyā nu matibhramo nu

details.body: Or, conj. aTavA, yadvA, vA (never at beginning) repeated after each word, or after the last; (in questions) nu, (svapno nu mAyA nu matiBramo nu); uta, Aho, Ahosvit (correl. of kiM ‘whether’). 2 anyaTA, itaraTA, aTavA, nocet.

OR: I In gen.: vA, whether child or pupil: SiSurvA SizyA vA, U. iv. 11.; whether God is spoken of in this passage or not: kiM brahmAsmin vAkye'BiDIyate na veti, S. ii. 15.; from fear of the king or of thieves: rAjaBayAccOramayAdvA, Mr. iii.; or else: kiM vA, Vi. vi. 21. (when=other- -wise: nocet, H.).II In interrogation direct or implied: is it a dream, an illusion, or delusion of my mind: svapno nu mAyA nu matiBramo nu, Sa.; is my strength gone or am I another: DvastaM nu me vIryamutAhamanyaH, Ki.; or is (she) going to live with hinds: Aho nivatsyati samaM hariRANga- nABiH, Sa.; shall I kill him, or is he dream- ing: kiM vyApAdayAmyutotsvapnAyate, Mr. iii.; I do not know whether this is becoming of (your) bark or (your) matted hair, whether it befits (your) penances or it is a part of (your) religi- ous observances: na jAne kimidaM valkalAnAM sadfSamu- tAho jawAnAM samucitaM, kiM tapaso'nurUpamAhosvidDarmakarmA- padeSANgamidam, K. (N. B. nu is interro. and not used in such cases).III Beginning a sentence: aTavA, or to injure tender things: aTavA mfdu vastu hiMsitum, R. viii. 45.IV In defi- -nitions or explanations: by ca or not expr., is called a fratricide or a brother-killer: BrAtfhA BrAtfGAtI cABiDIyate.
OR , conj. vA placed after a word, vApi, aTavA, yadvA; ‘friend or foe,’ mitraM vA Satrur vA. — (Or else) aTavA, kiMvA, anyaTA, itaraTA, Ahosvit.

Oracle, s. dEvI vAk, deva-AkASa-vARI, AkASaBavA-aSarIriRI-sarasvatI. 2 praSna-devatA-devaH. 3 praSna-Sakuna-sTAnaM. 4 pramARaM, AptaH, pramARapuruzaH; AptavacanaM. Oracular, a. devavARItulya, pramARaBUta, Apta, prAmA-Rika (kI f.).
ORACLE: I Lit.:(1) dEvavARI;(2) dEvI vAk; (3) AkASaBavA sarasvatI (from heaven); and sim. comp.s.II A prophet: q. v.: Bavizya- dvaktA (m.).

ORACLE , s. (Answer of a god to an inquiry made) SakunaM -naH, praSnaH, prasAdaH; ‘through a voice,’ devavARI, AkASavARI. — (The deity who gives the answer) praSnadevatA, prasAdadevatA, praSnadevaH, SakunadevaH. — (The place where the answer is given) praSnasTAnaM, SakunasTAnaM, prasAdasTAnaM. — (A person whose opinion is of great authority) pramARaM, AptaH. — (A wise or authoritative sentence) AptavacanaM, AptoktiH f.
ORACULAR: (1) expr. with subs., his words are o.: *dEvavARIsannimastasya byAhAraH;(2) prAmARikaH (kI, kaM) (= authoritative).

ORACULAR , ORACULOUS, a. SAkunikaH -kI -kaM, SAkunaH -nI -naM, Saku- nadaH -dA -daM. — (Like an oracle) devavARItulyaH -lyA -lyaM, devavARI- sadfSaH -SI -SaM. — (Authoritative) prAmARikaH -kI -kaM, AptaH -ptA -ptaM. — (Obscure) gUQArTaH -rTA -rTaM.
ORACULARLY , adv. devavARIpUrvvaM, devavARIsAdfSyena, saSakunaM.
Oral, a. vAcika (kI f.), ukta, aliKita; ‘o(ral) message’ vAcikaM. [Oral]ly, adv. vAcA, muKadvArA, aliKitaM.
ORAL: (1) vAcikaH (kI, kaM) (= verbal), I now wish to know his o. (communication): vAcika- midAnIM SrotumicCAmi, Mu. v.;(2) mOKikaH (kI, kaM) (lit. but ambiguous).
ORAL , a. (Spoken by the mouth, not written) muKatIyaH -yA -yaM, uktaH -ktA -ktaM, aliKitaH -tA -taM, muKakaTitaH -tA -taM, SrutaH -tA -taM.
ORALLY: vAcA (= in words) and sim. comp.s.
ORALLY , adv. muKatas, muKAt -Kena, aliKitaM, muKadvArA.
ORANG-OUTANG: vanamAnuzaH (?), K.
Orange, s. nAraMgaH, nAgaraMgaH, ErAvataH, nAdeyI, BUmijaMbukA; (fruit) nAraMgaPalaM; ‘o(range)-coloured’ picCila, kOsuMBa (BI f.). Orangery, s. nAgaraMga-vAwikA.
ORANGE: I The fruit:(1) nAgaraNgam;(2) maDu- jambIram (use m. for the tree).II The colour: raktapItaH.

ORANGE , s. (Tree) nAraNgaH, nAgaraNgaH, nAryyaNgaH, suraNgaH, tvagganDaH, danta- SaWaH, ErAvataH, kirmmIraH, colakI m. (n), latAtaruH m., nAdeyaH, BUmijambukA, rAjaPaRijJakaH. — (The fruit) nAraNgaPalaM, nAgaraNgaPalaM, picCilaH.
ORANGE-COLORED , a. nAraNgavarRaH -rRA -rRaM, kOsumBaH -mBI -mBaM, picCilavarRaH &c.
ORANGE-PEEL , s. picCilatvak m. (c), nAraNgaPalatvak m. (c).
ORANGERY: nAgaraNgavAwikA (?).
ORANGERY , s. nAraNgavfkzavAwikA, nAraNgataruvAwikA.

Oration, s. vAkprabaMDaH, sAlaMkAraM vacanaM, pravacanaM, sarasvatInizyaMdaH (‘fluent o(ration)’). Orator, s. pra-, vaktf m., vAkSOMqaH-caturaH, pravacanapawuH, sadvaktf m. vAkpawuH, vAgmin m., vAgISaH, vAkpaMqitaH-viSAradaH; saBApaMqitaH. [Orator]ical, a. vAkcAturyamaya (yI f.), sAlaM-kAra, vAgalaMkAramaya. [Orator]y, s. vAgmitA, vAkpAwavaM-cAturyaM, suvaktftvaM, vAkSakti f., vaktftvaM, saBApAMqityaM. 2 prArTanAgAraM, upA-sanAsTAnaM, BajanAlayaH. Oratorio, s. tAlabadDaM DarmakIrtanaM. 2 Oratory q. v.
ORATION: vaktftA (used in Bengali); prOQavyAhAraH (?); sarasvatInisyandaH (?).
ORATION , s. vAkprabanDaH, vAkyaprabanDaH, vAkyaM, pravacanaM, sAlaNkAravAkyaM, sAlaNkAraBAzaRaM, sopapattikavAkya, alaNkAramayaM vAkyaM.
ORATOR: (1) vAkyakovidaH (?);(2) vaktf (m.) (= speaker).

ORATOR , s. (Public declaimer) saBAvaktA m. (ktf), saBApravaktA m., saBA- vAdI m. (n), saBApaRqitaH, vaktA m., pravaktA m., vAdI m., pravacana- karttA m. — (Eloquent speaker) vAkpawuH m., pravacanapawuH m., suva- ktA m., sadvaktA m., vAgISaH, vAgISvaraH, vAkpaRqitaH, vAgvid m., vAgvidagDaH, saBApaRqitaH, vAgviSAradaH, vAkyadvAreRa vismayajanakaH.
ORATORICAL: by comp., or talents: vaktftA- SaktiH (?).

ORATORICAL , a. vAgalaNkAramayaH -yI -yaM, vANmayaH -yI -yaM, vAkcAturyyamayaH &c., sAlaNkAravAkyamayaH &c., saBAvaktftvasambanDI &c., saBApARqityasambanDI &c., saBApARqityavizayaH -yA -yaM, pravacanasambanDI &c.
ORATORIO: *gItasandarBaH.
ORATORIO , s. tAlabadDaM DarmmakIrttanaM, DarmmakIrttanavizayA susvararacanA or susvarasaNgaH.
ORATORY: I The art:(1) vAgmitA (?);(2) vAkpAwavam (?).II A place of prayer: *BajanAlayam.

ORATORY , s. (Art of public speaking) saBAvaktftvaM, saBApravacanavidyA, saBApravacanaM, saBApravacanapARqityaM, saBApARqityaM. — (Art of speaking eloquently) vAkpawutA, pravacanapawutA, suvaktftvaM, sadvaktftA, vaktftvaSaktiH f., vAkSaktiH f., vAkcAturyyaM, SabdacAturyyaM, vAcASaktiH f., vAcoyuktiH f., SabdapARqityaM, supralApaH. — (Place for prayer) prArTanAgAraM, prArTanasTAnaM.

Orb, s. maMqalaH-laM, biMbaH-baM, vartulaM, cakraM, vfttaM, golaH-laM; ‘the moon with entire (undiminished) o(rb)’ pUrRa-avikala-maMqalaH caMdraH, aKaMqakalaH SaSI (Mal. 2). [Orb]ed, Orbicular, a. maMqalAkAra, vartula, golAkfti. Orbiculate, s. vartulaM. a. vartula; See (s.).
ORB (subs.): maRqalam: v. Circle, disk.
ORB (v.): I Lit.: maRqalIkaroti.II Fig.: maRqayati (= to adorn: q. v.).
ORB , s. maRqalaM, golaH -laM, golakaH, varttulaM, vimbaH -mbaM, vimbakaM, parimaRqalaM, cakraM, cakravAlaM, vfttaM, valayaH -yaM; ‘circular array,’ cakravyUhaH.
ORBATE , a. vihInaH -nA -naM, hInaH -nA -naM, mAtfpitfhInaH &c.
ORBED (adj.): maRqalin (f. nI): v. Circular, round.

ORBED , ORBICULAR, ORBICULATE, a. maRqalAkAraH -rA -raM, maRqalAkftiH -tiH -ti, golAkAraH &c., maRqalI -linI -li (n), vimbI &c., varttulaH -lA -laM, varttulAkAraH &c., cakrAkAraH &c., cAkrikaH -kI -kaM, cakrI &c., cAkreyaH -yI -yaM.
ORBICULARLY , adv. maRqalAkAreRa, golAkAreRa, varttularUpeRa, cakravat.
ORBICULARNESS , s. maRqalAkAratA, golAkAratA, maRqalatA, varttulatA.
Orbit, s. kakzA-kzaH, grahapaTaH-mArgaH.
ORBIT: kakzA, o. of a planet: grahakakzA, Su. xii. 73.
ORBIT , s. (Of a planet) kakzA -kzaH, grahapaTaH, grahamArgaH, maRqalaM; ‘apex of an orbit, uccaH; ‘apsis,’ mandoccaH.
Orchard, s. vAwikA, vAwaH-wI, upavanaM, vfkzodyAnaM, vfkzavAwikA; ‘fruit o(rchard)’ puzpa-vAwikA.
ORCHARD: PalavAwikA (?), mango-o.: AmravAwikA, -vanam and so on.
ORCHARD , s. vfkzavAwikA, PalavfkzavAwI, taruvAwikA, vAwikA, vAwaH -wI -waM, upavanaM, vfkzodyAnaM, PalavfkzodyAnaM.
Orchestra, s. vAditrasTAnaM-sTalaM. 2 vAdaka-samUhaH, vAditragaRaH.
ORCHESTRA: I Part of a theatre: vAditraBUmiH (??).II The body of musical performers: vAditravAdakAH (m. pl (??).
ORCHESTRA , s. (Place for musicians) vAditrasTAnaM, vAdyaBARqasTAnaM, vAditrasTalaM, BARqavAdakasTAnaM. — (Body of musicians) BARqavAda- kagaRaH, vAditrasamudAyaH, vAdyaBARqaM, vAdakasamUhaH.
ORCHESTRAL , a. vAdyaBARqasambanDI &c., vAdakagaRasambanDI &c.
ORCHID: *kozalatA.

Ordain, v. t. vi-DA 3 U, AdiS 6 P, nirdiS, saMvyavasTA c. (sTApayati), pra-pari-kxp c.; pracud 10, vac 2 P, smf 1 P; ‘o(rdain)ed by Sastras’ SAstrokta, SAstravihita-smfta, SAstranirdizwa, &c. 2 (aDikAre) niyuj 7 A, 10, aDikf 8 U or c., aBi-zic 6 P, vyA-diS; (religiously) dIkz 1 A, DarmakarmaRi niyuj. [Ordain]er, s. prakalpakaH, saMsTApakaH, pracodakaH.
ORDAIN: (1) niyojayati (yuj c. 10.): v. To employ;(2) AdiSati (diS, c. 6.): v. To order.

To ORDAIN , v. a. (Institute) viDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM), aBiDA, kxp (c. 10. kalpayati -yituM), prakxp, parikxp, sTA in caus. (sTApayati -yituM), pratizWA, saMsTA, vyavasTA, pracud (c. 10. -codayati -yituM), AdiS (c. 6. -diSati -dezwuM), sandiS, nirdiS. — (Appoint) niyuj (c. 7. -yunakti -yuMkte -yoktuM, c. 10. -yojayati -yituM), aDikf, prakf, samAdiS, vyAdiS. — (To any office) aDikAre or pade niyuj or aBizic (c. 6. -ziYcati -zektuM), niyojanaM kf, aDikftaM -tAM kf. — (Invest with sacer- dotal functions) DarmmADikAre or Darmmapade niyuj, DarmmADikArayuktaM kf, DarmmapadaniyuktaM kf, dIkz (c. 1. dIkzate -kzituM), dIkzAM kf, dIkzAka- rmmapUrvvaM DarmmADikAraM praviS (c. 10. -veSayati -yituM), DarmmapadadIkzitaM kf.

ORDAINED , p. p. (Instituted, established) vihitaH -tA -taM, kalpitaH -tA -taM, prakalpitaH &c., sTApitaH &c., pratizWApitaH, vyavasTApitaH &c., vyavasTitaH &c., coditaH &c., pracoditaH &c., nirdizwaH -zwA -zwaM, niya- mitaH &c., niyataH &c. — (Appointed) niyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, niyojitaH -tA -taM, aDikftaH -tA -taM, yojitaH -tA -taM. — (To any office) aDi- kAre or pade niyuktaH &c., aDikArayuktaH &c., aBiziktaH &c. — (To sacerdotal functions) DarmmADikAre niyuktaH &c., DarmmapadaniyuktaH, DarmmADikArayuktaH, DarmmapadadIkzitaH, dIkzitaH.
ORDAINER , s. prakalpakaH, viDAtA m. (tf), viDAyI m. (n), viDAyakaH, sTApakaH, pracodakaH, niyojakaH, yojakaH.
Ordeal, s. divyaM, satyaM, parIkzA, pramARaM; ‘o(rdeal) by fire’ koSaH-zaH, taptadivyaM; ‘subjecting, oneself to o(rdeal)’ divyagrahaRaM; ‘trying o(rdeal)’ (fig.) tattvanikazA Apad.

ORDEAL: I Lit.: here the o. s for clearing (one- self) are by balance, by fire, by water, by poison, by drinking divine water: tulAgnavApo vizaM kozo divyAnIha viSudDaye, Y. ii. 97.; to accept an o.: divyaM karoti, V. s.II Fig., severe trial: expr. with vyasanam or vipad (= calamity: q. v.).

ORDEAL , s. parIkzA, DarmmADarmmaparIkzA, divyaM, satyaM, pramARaM, kozaH -zaM, koSaH, SApaH, SapaTaH, SapanaM, pratyayaH, kriyA; ‘fiery ordeal,’ agni- parIkzA, taptadivyaM; ‘ordeal of the balance,’ tulAparIkzA, tulAkoSaH; ‘purification by ordeal,’ kozaSudDiH f.; ‘the act of under- going an ordeal,’ divyagrahaRaM, divyakaraRaM, kozagrahaRaM; ‘that under- goes one,’ divyakArI -riRI -ri (n), kozagrAhI &c.; ‘to undergo one,’ kozaM or satyaM or divyaM kf; ‘proved by ordeal,’ SApitaH -tA -taM.

Order, v. t. AdiS 6 P, nir-ni-samA-vyA-diS, SAs 2 P, A-jYA c. (jYApayati), pracud 10. 2 vi-DA 3 U, praRI 1 P, nirvah c.; See Manage. 3 parikxp c., krameRa vinyas 4 U or c. or sTA c. (sTApayati) or ni-DA, saMvi-DA, vyavasTA c., vi-, rac 10; vyUh 1 U. 4 Ordain, q. v. s. AjYA, A-ni-deSaH, nirdeSaH, SAsanaM, niyogaH; ‘written o(rder)’ AjYApatraM; ‘what are your o(rder)s’ ko niyogo'nuzWIyatAM; ‘your Majestyʼs o(rder)s will be obeyed’ yaTAjYApayati devaH. 2 pra-, codanaM-nA, viDiH, niyamaH, viDAnaM, preraRA, vacanaM. 3 kramaH, anukramaH, paripAwi-wI f., AnupUrvyaM-rvI, paryAyaH, paraMparA, pAraMparyaM, Avft f.; vyavasTA, vinyAsaH, viracanaM-nA, saMviDAnaM; ‘natural o(rder)’ AnulomyaM; ‘inverted o(rder)’, ‘reverse o(rder)’ prAtilomyaM, vyutkramaH, vyatikramaH, viparyayaH, viparyAsaH, vyatyAsaH, vyatyayaH; ‘o(rder) of battle’ vyUhaH, sEnyaracanA, balavinyAsaH; ‘natural o(rder) of words’ anvayaH; ‘in natural or direct o(rder)’ anulomaM-mataH; ‘in inverted o(rder)’ pratilomaM-mataH; ‘in good o(rder)’ susTita, surakzita, suvihita; ‘in o(rder)’ suvinyasta, suviracita, vyavasTita, krameRa sTApita; (adv.) krameRa, kramaSaH, yaTAkramaM, kramAnurUpaM, anupUrvaSaH, AnupUrvyeRa, paripAwyA; ‘in o(rder) to’ ex. by arTe-rTaM in comp.; by dat. or by inf.; ‘out of o(rder)’ avyavasTita, Bagna-krama, asusTa. 4 mArgaH, sTiti f., rIti f., padDati f., AcAraH, niyamaH; ‘not breaking the (established) o(rder)’ sTiteraBettA (R. iii. 27) sTityE daMqayato daMqyAn (R. i. 25) ‘for maintaining o(rder) &c.’; ‘breaking the o(rder)’ sTitiBedaH, atipAtaH, paryayaH, upAtyayaH. 5 gaRaH, vargaH, varRaH, jAti f.; ‘the lower o(rder)s’ avara-aDama-varRAH, aMtyavargaH, aDamajAtIyAH. 6 ASramaH, varRA-SramaH; ‘head of a religious o(rder)’ ASrama-guruH. [Order]er, s. AjYApakaH, Adezwf m.; SAstf m. [Order]less, a. kramahIna, SUnya, akrama, anavasTitaM. [Order]ly, a. vyavasTita, yaTAkrama, kramAnugata, sakrama, anupUrva. adv. yaTAkramaM, paryAyeRa, kramaSaH.

ORDER (subs.): I Disposition, arrangement: q. v.: (I) kramaH (of succession), without devia- ting from o.: anujPitakramaH, Ku.; in regular o.: yaTAkramam;(2) paripAwI, M. n. Ph.: o. of battle: vyUhaH; without o.: ucCfNgalam.II Regularity: q. v.: paripAwI. Ph.: in o. (as of the organs:) prakftisTa (f. sTA).III Established usage:(1) sTitiH, observer of o.: sBiteraBettA, R. iii. 27. or aBinna- sTitiH, Sa. v. 11.;(2) maryAdA, M. n.IV A command, direction:(1) AjYA, sending me o. s: prezayanmahyamAjYAm, Mu. ii.: received his o. with pleasure: tadAjYAM mudito'grahIt, R. xii. 7.; to give an o.: AjYAM dadAti, Ku.;(2) AdeSaH or nideSaH, getting their master's o.: BarturAdeSaM samavApya, Ki. vi. 46.; I wish to know (his) o.: nideSaM jYAtumicCAmi, Mah.;(3) niyogaH, (we) have carried out (our) preceptor's o.: anuzWito gurUniyogaH, Sa.;(4) SAsanam, to stand by an o.: SAsane tizWati, R. xi. 65.V For paying money: SAsanam, nideSaH, etc. may be used.VI Rank, class: SreRiH (RI). Ph.: the lower o. s: prAkftAH or pfTagjanAH (m. pl.).VII Of religious com- -munities: sampradAyaH.VIII For constructing houses: viDAnam (?).IX In pl., to take (holy) o. s.: *AcAryakzetraM praviSati or AcAryatvaM parigfhnAti. Ph.: (a) in o. to read, etc. (i. e. for the pur- -pose of): aDyayanArTam or aDyayanAya: v. For; (b) o. of the day: dEnikakramaH (?).

ORDER (v.): I To arrange, dispose: q. v.: parikalpayati (kxp, c. 10.).II To command, direct:(2) A-diSati, ni-, samA-, (diS, c. 6.), I have been o. ed by the Princess of Benares: Adizwo'smi kASirAjaputryA, V. iii.;(2) AjYApayati, sam-, (c. of jYA), as your Majesty o. s.: yadAjYA- payati devaH, Mah.; o. the forces to eradicate (his) resolution: saMkalpasamunmUlanAya daRqacakramAjYApaya, Mah. i.;(3) SAsti (SAs, c. 2 (ambiguous).

ORDER , s. (Regular disposition, arrangement) kramaH, anukramaH, paryyAyaH, AnupUrvyaM, AnupUrvI, paripAwI -wiH f., pAripAwyaM, vinyAsaH, vyUhanaM, vyUQiH f., Avft f., pAramparyyaM, paramparA, vyavasTA, vyavasTApanaM, krameRa sTApanaM, prativiDAnaM, saMviDAnaM, viracanaM -nA; ‘inverted order,’ vyatikramaH, vyutkramaH; ‘natural order of words,’ anvayaH. — (Esta- blished mode of proceeding) kramaH, mArgaH, rItiH f., niynamaH, padDatiH f.; ‘direct order,’ AnulomyaM; ‘in direct order,’ anulomaH -mA -maM; ‘inverse order,’ prAtilomyaM; ‘in inverse order,’ pratilomaH -mA -maM, vilomaH &c. — (Command) AjYA, [Page556-a+ 51] AdeSaH, nideSaH, nirdeSaH, SAsanaM, SizwiH f., SAstiH f., niyogaH, preraRA, avavAdaH, prayuktiH f. — (Precept, rule) niyamaH, codanaM -nA, viDiH m., viDAnaM, vacanaM; ‘written order,’ AjYApatraM, SAsanapatraM; ‘general order,’ sAmAnyaSAsanaM, sADAraRAjYA. — (Class, grade) gaRaH, vargaH, varRaH, jAtiH f.; ‘the lower orders,’ avaravarRAH m. pl., aDamavarRAH, prAkftavargaH, antyavargaH, antyajAtIyAH m. pl., aDamajAtIyAH m. pl.; ‘the middle or common order,’ sAmAnyavargaH, sAmAnyapakzaH, sADAraRapakzaH. — (Religious order) ASramaH. There are four Āśramas, corresponding to the four stages of the Brahman's life. Every Brahman who has passed through these four stages is supposed to have passed through the four orders in succession. When, in the first, he is called brahmacArI m.; in the 2d, gfhasTaH; in the 3d, vAnaprasTaH or vEKAnasaH or yatI; in the 4th, BikzuH m., sannyAsI m. The first order, or that of the religious student, is also called liNgaM. Other terms, expressive of religious orders, are parAyaRaM, mArgaH, sampradAyaH, panTAH m. (paTin); ‘head of a religious order,’ ASramaguruH m. — (In good order, in proper state) susTaH -sTA -sTaM, susTitaH -tA -taM, surakzitaH -tA -taM. — (In order, properly arranged) suvinyastaH -stA -staM, suracitaH -tA -taM, suvyavasTitaH -tA -taM, krameRa sTApitaH -tA -taM; ‘in regular order,’ yaTAkramaM, krameRa -mAt, kramaSas, anupUrvvaSas, anukramaSas, suparipAWyA. — (In order to, for the purpose) arTaM or arTe affixed; as, ‘in order to read,’ aDyayanArTaM, or expressed by the dat. c.; as, ‘in order to find a fourth quantity,’ caturTarASer avagamAya. — (Out of order) avyavasTitaH -tA -taM, anavasTitaH &c., BagnakramaH -mA -maM, asusTaH -sTA -sTaM, asvasTaH &c.

To ORDER , v. a. (sTApayati -yituM), vyavasTA. — (Command) AjYA in caus. (-jYApayati -yituM), samAjYA, AdiS (c. 6. -diSati -dezwuM), samAdiS, sandiS, vyAdiS, pratisandiS, prakxp, kxp, cud (c. 10. codayati -yituM), aBicud, prer (c. 10. -Irayati -yituM), SAs (c. 2. ORGAN: I A medium:(1) indriyam (of men), the o. of taste: rasanendriyam, D.;(2) karaRam, there are three internal and ten external o. s: antaH- karaRatrayaM daSa bAhyakaraRAni, S. p. b. Ph.: the male o.: liNgam; the female o.: yoniH.II Fig.: dvAram.III A musical instrument: *ArgaRam.

ORGAN , s. (Instrument of action) sADanaM, karmmasADanaM, karaRaM, upa- karaRaM, kAraRaM. — (Organ of action) karmmendriyaM. Of these, five are given: 1. ‘the larynx or voice,’ vAk f. (c); 2. ‘the hand,’ pARiH m.; 3. ‘the foot,’ pAdaH; 4. ‘the organ of ex- cretion,’ pAyuH m.; 5. ‘of generation,’ upasTaH. — (Organ of sense or perception) indriyaM, jYAnendriyaM, jYAnasADanaM, vizayi n. (n), hfzIkaM. Of these, five are reckoned: 1. ‘the eye,’ cakzus; 2. ‘the ear,’ SrotraM; 3. ‘the nose,’ GrARaM: 4. ‘the tongue,’ jihvA; 5. ‘the skin,’ tvak f. (c). The word indriyaM may be af- fixed to any of these; as, ‘the organ of sight,’ cakzuri- ndriyaM &c.; for the corresponding vizaya or ‘objects of sense,’ see OBJECT. — (Internal organ, or organ of the in- tellect) antarindriyaM, DIndriyaM. Of these, four are enumerated: 1. ‘the mind, or organ of thought,’ manas; 2. ‘apprehension,’ budDiH f.; 3. ‘individuality, or sense of self,’ ahaNkAraH; 4. ‘feel- ing,’ cittaM. In opposition to the ‘internal organs,’ the [Page557-a+ 51] organs of perception and action are sometimes called ‘external organs,’ vahirindriyARi. The organs collectively, indriyagrAmaH, indriyavargaH. — (Instrument, or means of communi- cation) dvAraM, sADanaM. — (Musical instrument) vaMSI, suziravaMSapUrRavAdyaM.
ORGANIC: by comp., o. pleasure: indriyasuKam. Ph.: o. substance: *vyUQapadArTaH.

(-sTApayati -yituM), nirmA (c. 2. -mAti, c. 3. -mimIte -mAtuM), Gaw (c. 10. (n), jAtiH f., AgamaH, upakramaH. — (Source, foun- tain) AdiH m., yoniH m. f., mUlaM, vIjaM, hetuH m., kAraRaM, Adi- kAraRaM, garBaH, nibanDanaM, nidAnaM, utpattisTAnaM, udgamasTAnaM. — (Original instigator) prayojakaH, pravarttakaH; ‘of low origin,’ duryoniH -niH -ni, hInayoniH &c., hInajAtiH -tiH -ti, hInajanmA -nmA -nma (n); ‘of noble origin,’ mOlaH -lI -laM, utkfzwajAtiH &c., uttamavaMSajAtaH -tA -taM; ‘prosperity has its origin in the king,’ rAjamUlA sampattiH.

ORIGINAL (adj.): I Primitive: q. v.: AdimaH (mA, maM).II Primary: mUla- in comp., o. side (of a High Court): *mUlavimAgaH.II Not translated or borrowed: expr. with: mUlam. IV Having new ideas, etc.: perh. ananya- sADAraRa (f. RI): v. Also originality.
ORIGINAL (subs.): Origin: q. v. II An o. work: mUlam, this is just like the o.: yaTA mUlaM taTEvEtat, K. s. 1. 10.III First copy: mUlam.
ORIGINAL , s. (Origin). See the preceding. (First copy, archetype) AdarSaH, pratyupamAnaM, pratyupamA, mUlaM, mUlapatraM. — (Text) mUlaM, mUlagranTaH.

(Primitive, first in order) mOlaH -lI -laM, mOlikaH -kI -kaM, mUlikaH -kA -kaM, praTamaH -mA -maM, prATamikaH -kI -kaM, AdyaH -dyA -dyaM, AdimaH -mA -maM Adi in comp., pUrvvaH -rvvI -rvvaM. — (Not made or done before, or by another) apUrvvaH -rvvA -rvvaM, apUrvva- karttfkaH -kA -kaM, apUrvvasidDaH -dDA -dDaM, apUrvvaracitaH -tA -taM, apUrvvapratimaH -mA -maM, svayaNkftaH &c., svayaNkalpitaH &c., svataHkalpitaH &c. — (Hav- ing the power to originate new thoughts) apUrvvakalpakaH -kA -kaM, svayaNkalpakaH &c., svataHkalpakaH &c., apUrvvayojakaH &c., anuyogI &c.

(n), pratikarmma, prasADanaM, raYjanaM, kalpanA, sajjA, raNgaH, nepaTyaM. — (That which ornaments, an ornament) alaNkAraH, BUzaRaM, ABaraRaM, BaraRaM, kaNkaRaH -RaM, kalApaH, aNgadaM; ‘ornament of language,’ alaNkAraH, SabdAlaNkAraH; of sense,’ arTAlaNkAraH; ‘for the feet or ankles,’ nUpuraH -raM, pAdANgadaM.

(Bereaved of both parents) mAtfpitfhInaH -nA -naM, mAtApitfhInaH &c., pitAmAtfhInaH &c., mAtfpitfvihInaH &c., mAtApitfByAM vihInaH &c., mAtfpitfrahitaH &c. — (Bereaved of father) pitfhInaH -nA -naM, pitfvihInaH &c., pitrA vihInaH, mftapitfkaH -kA -kaM, gatapitfkaH &c., apitfkaH &c., anATaH -TA -TaM, nirnATaH &c., CemaRqaH, CamaRqaH. — (Of mother) mAtfhInaH -nA -naM, amAtfkaH -kA -kaM, mAtf- rahitaH -tA -taM, mftamAtfkaH -kA -kaM, gatamAtfkaH &c., hInamAtfkaH &c.

Ostracise, v. t. vi-nir-vas c. Ostracism, s. vivAsanaM, nirvAsanaM.
OSTRACISE: pravrAjayati (c. of vraj): v. To banish.
OSTRACISM: pravrAjanam: v. Banishment.
OSTRICH: *mahAdvijaH; KagozwraH.
OSTRICH , s. The word SahAmfgaH may be used.

Other, a. anya, apara, itara, para, anyatara (pron. a.); aMtaraM in comp. 2 Binna, vyatirikta. 3 ava-, Sizwa ‘the o(ther)s’ apare, anye, itare, SizwajanAH; ‘at o(ther) times’ anyadA; ‘the o(ther) day’ anyedyuH, nAticiraM. Wise, adv. anyaTA, itaraTA. 2 vA, na-no-cet, anyaTA, aTavA.

OTHER: (1) anyaH (nyA, -nyat), these and many others: ete cAnye ca bahavaH, D. b.; by any o. (individual): tvadanyena, R. iii. 63.; at o. times: anyadA, R. xi. 78.; in o. places: anyatra, R. xiii. 56.; no. o.: nAnyaditaH kiYcit, D. vii.; (2) aparaH (rA, raM), the o. went to Vidarbha: yayAvaparo vidarBAn, R. v. 60.; but o. s blamed: apare tu nininduH, D. iv.; the o. end: aparAntaH, R. iv. 58.;(3) itaraH (rA, rat) (= all o.: rare), of the o. s: itarezAm, S.; not fit for any o. (man): itarasmE na yogyA, D. v. Ph.: (a) o.'s: para- in comp.: v. Another.; (b) belonging to o. s.: (1) anyadIyaH (yA, yaM);(2) parakIyaH (yA, yaM); (c) the o. day: tasmin divase (comp. Beng.).

OTHER , a. anyaH -nyA -nyat, itaraH -rA -raM, paraH -rA -raM, aparaH -rA -raM, anyadIyaH -yA -yaM, anyataraH -rA -rat, parakIyaH -yA -yaM, vyatiriktaH -ktA -ktaM antaraM in comp.; ‘other's wealth,’ paraDanaM, anyaDanaM; ‘other [Page559-a+ 51] kings,’ rAjAntarARi n. pl.; ‘the other world,’ paralokaH -kaM, aparalokaH; ‘the other day,’ anyadivase, anyasmin divase, anye- dyus; ‘on the other side,’ aparatas; ‘on the other hand,’ paratas, anyatra, parapakze. — (Different) BinnaH -nnA -nnaM, viBinnaH &c., aparaH -rA -raM, anyaH -nyA -nyat, ekaH -kA -kaM, tvaH -tvA -tvaM; ‘other than this,’ etadBinnaH &c.; ‘he has no other business than reading the Vedas,’ vedADyayanAt tasya kAryyaM nAnyat. — (Each other) parasparaH -rA -raM, anyonyaH -nyA -nyaM, itaretaraH -rA -raM. — (Rest) SizwaH -zwA -zwaM, avaSizwaH &c.; ‘the others,’ SizwajanAH m. pl., apare m. pl.
OTHERWHERE , adv. anyatra, itaratra, aparatra, paratra, sTAnAntare.

OTHERWISE: I Differently: anyaTA, what should not be done o.: nAnyaTA yadDi kartavyam, Mah. iii. 1. 34.; if I speak o.: anyaTA ced bravImyaham, V. p. iv. 13. 60.II In other respects: perh. anyaTA; anyAnya- or aparAparavizayezu (?). III = or else:(1) na (no) cet, o. I would kill you: no cedDantavyo'si mayA, H.;(2) viparIte (= on the contrary), Mah. iii. 10. 36.; (3) anyaTA, Da.

OTHERWISE , adv. (In a different manner) anyaTA, itaraTA, paratas. — (In other ways) anyaDA, anyaprakArEH, anyaviDena. — (Or else) aTavA, anyaTA, kiMvA, no cet, na cet, aneva; ‘but not other- wise,’ na tvanyaTA.
Otiose, a. anavahita, nirutsAha, pramatta, avyApfta.
OTTAR , OTTO, s. (Of rose) javApuzyaniryyAsaH, oqrapuzpaniryyUhaH.
Otter, s. udraH, jalamArjAraH.
OTTER: (1) udraH (best equiv.);(2) jalaviqAlaH and sim. comp.s.
OTTER , s. (The animal) udraH jalamArjAraH, jalanakulaH, pAnIyanakulaH, nIrajaH, nIrAKuH m.
OTTOMAN: I A Turk: turUzkaH. Ph.: the O. empire: turUzkasAmrAjyam.II A couch: *turUzka- Sayanam.
Ought, v. Ex. by arh 1 P; gen. by pot. pass. part. or by pot.; See Must.

OUGHT: (1) arhati (often = please), impatience o. not to lead you away from political success: na BavantamakzamA nayasidDerapanetumarhati, Ki. ii. 42.;(2) by -tavya, -anIya and -ya part. s, I o. to do that: mayA tat kartavyam: v. Should.

OUGHT , v. irreg. (Be bound, be obliged, be necessary) ex- pressed by the fut. pass. part.; as, ‘you ought to marry the damsel,’ tvayA kanyA voQavyA; ‘we ought to restrain an- ger,’ asmABiH kopaH niyantavyaH; ‘I ought not to do that,’ mayA tat na karttavyaM or karaRIyaM or kAryyaM, or sometimes by the po- tential mood; as, ‘he ought to treat his son like a friend,’ putraM mitravad Acaret, or by the use of the verb arh; as, ‘he ought to give,’ dAtum arhati; ‘to act as one ought,’ yaTo- citaM or yaTAyogyaM or yaTArhaM kf.
Ounce, s. waMkadvayaM, paRArDaM. 2 dvIpin m.
OUNCE: I A weight = waNkadvayam (in Troy weight); = paRArdDam (of gold, silver, etc.). II An animal: dvIpin (m.).
OUNCE , s. (Weight) palaM, ardDawaNkaH, waNkArdDaM. — (Animal) dvIpI m. (n).
OUR, OURS: (1) asmadIyaH (yA, yaM);(2) by gen.: v. Also our. N. B. After not expr.: v. My.

OUR , a. asmAkaM gen. c. pl. (asmat), asmadIyaH -yA -yaM asmad pre- fixed; as, ‘our country,’ asmAkaM deSaH or asmadIyadeSaH or asma- ddeSaH; ‘our own’ is expressed by Atma in comp.; as, ‘our own country,’ AtmadeSaH.
OURANG-OUTANG , s. manuzpaSarIraH kapiBedaH.

OURSELVES , pron. reciprocal, expressed by AtmA m. (n) or by Atma in comp. or by svayaM in comp.; ‘we will kill ourselves,’ vayam Atmano hanizyAmaH; ‘done by ourselves,’ AtmakftaH -tA -taM; ‘we ourselves,’ te vayaM.
OUSEL: a bird: *aYjanaH; nIlapakzaH.
Oust, v. t. niHsf c., nizkas c., apAs 4 U, nirAkf 8 U, bahizkf; See Dispel, Drive out.
OUST: niHsArayati (c. of sf): v. To drive out, expel.
To OUST v. a. niHsf (c. 10. -sArayati -yituM), vahizkf, vihiHkf, nirAkf, apAs (c. 4. -asyati -asituM), niras, sTAnAd BraMS (c. 10. BraMSayati -yituM), nizkas (c. 10. -kAsayati -yituM),
OUSTED , p. p. niHsAritaH -tA -taM, vahizkftaH -tA -taM, sTAnaBrazwaH -zwA -zwaM.

Out, adv. bahiH (with abl.); ‘gone o(ut)’ bahirgata; (with verbs) ex. by nir, vi, apa, pra, bahiH; ‘to be o(ut)’ prakASatAM gam 1 P, prakASIBU 1 P; ‘the secret is o(ut)’ rahasyaM BinnaM. 2 nirvApita a.; ‘to be o(ut)’ praSam 4 P, nirvA 2 P; ‘the lamp was o(ut)’ dIpaH praSaSAma-nirvavO. 3 kzIRa-vigata-avasita a. 4 aMtaM-SezaM-yAvat, AvasAnAt; ‘hear me o(ut)’ SfRu me sAvaSezaM vacaH (M. 4); ‘let me speak o(ut)’ vacaH samA-payAni tAvat. 5 uccEH, ucca-tAra-svareRa, muktakaMWaM. 6 vyaktaM, prakawaM, spazwaM, sPuwaM; ‘o(ut) upon (with) the thief’ dUrIkriyatAM-niHsAryatAM-asA cOraH; ‘o(ut) of’ bahiH with abl., or by abl.; (among) maDyAt with gen., or by gen. or loc.; (exclusion) ex. by a, nir, vi, apa, gata, nazwa, tyakta in comp.; ‘o(ut) of the road’ tyakta-Brazwa-mArga; ‘o(ut) of oneʼs mind’ hata-nazwa-budDi, budDi-Brazwa; ‘o(ut) of place’ asTAna, anucita; ‘o(ut) of order’ utsUtra, kramahIna, viDivi-rudDa, avyavasTita; ‘o(ut) of tune’ apa-vi-svara; (showing motive) ex. by instr. or abl.; (beyond) atIta, agocara in comp., ati pr.; ‘o(ut) of sight’ nayana-vizayAtIta, dfgagocara, aMtarhita; ‘o(ut) of oneʼs reach’ avizaya, aprApya; ‘o(ut) of oneʼs power’ atiSakti; ‘o(ut) of use’ gata-lupta-vyavahAra, avyavahArita; ‘o(ut) of fashion’ lokAcAravirudDa, ‘o(ut) of time’ gatakAla, kAlAtita; ‘o(ut) of hope’ gatASa, nirASa; ‘o(ut) of manʼs strength’ ati-mAnuza; ‘to pass o(ut) of sight’ nayana-vizayaM ati-i 2 P or atikram 1 U, 4 P; ‘stand o(ut) of hearing’ SravaRAgocarastizWa; ‘o(ut) of employment’ kzIRavftti, nirvyApAra, niyogahIna; ‘o(ut) of office’ Brazwa-cyuta-aDi-kAra, aDikAraBrazwa-cyuta; ‘o(ut) of hand’ sadyaH, sapadi; ‘o(ut)-door’ dvArabahiHsTa, bahiHpradeSakfta; ‘o(ut)-house’ upagfhaM, bahirgfhaM. interj. apehi, apasara, Dik (with acc.). [Out]er, [Out]ermost, a. bAhya, bahiHsTa, bahirBava, ba-hirvartin, bahiH in comp. [Out]most, a. ati-bAhya. [Out]ward, a. bAhya, bahiH in comp. 2 dfSya, AvirBUta, prakawa, prakASa. 3 avAntava (vI f.), miTyA-mfzA in comp. adv. (‘O(utward)s’) bahiH, bahirBAge-deSe. [Out]wardly, adv. bAhyataH, bahiH, bahirBAge. 2 avastutaH, mfzA, miTyA, kftakaM, kftrimaM.

OUT (adj.): I Not within: bahis: v. The several verbs with which it is used.II Not at home: bahirgataH (tA, taM).III Pub- -lished: q. v.: bahirgataH (tA, taM).IV Dis- -closed: vivftaH (tA, taM).:V Extinguished, gone: gataH (tA, taM).VI Not in office: expr. with nAsti.VII Completely: q. v. VIII Perceptively: uccEH.IX In error: expr. with Bramati, vi- (Bram, c. 1.).X Un- -covered: anAvftaH (tA, taM).XI Away, off: q.v.: “o. with the dog”: dUrIkurU kukku ram.XII Openly: sPuwam.

OUT , adv. (Without, not in) vahis, nir, vi, vinir, apa pre- fixed, governing the abl. c.; ‘to go out,’ vahirgam, nirgam, vinirgam, apagam; ‘to draw out,’ nizkfz; ‘to be out,’ vahirBU; ‘having gone out into the open air,’ prakASaM nirgatya. — (De- noting disclosure or discovery) expressed by the prep. vi, apa, pra, pari, ni, nir, ava &c., in combination with various roots; as, ‘to give out,’ prakAS, vikAS, nivid, viGuz; ‘to find out,’ parijYA, aBijYA, nirUp, upalaB, nirRI; ‘to be out, be disclosed,’ vivftaH -tA -taM BU, prakASitaH -tA -taM BU; ‘the secret is out,’ rahasyaM BinnaM or viBinnaM or prakASitaM. — (Denoting extinc- [Page559-b+ 51] tion) expressed by nir, with the root vA; as, ‘to put out,’ nirvA in caus.; ‘to go out,’ nirvA, nirvARaH -RA -RaM BU. — (In a state of exhaustion or being empty) kzIRaH -RA -RaM, parikzIRaH -RA -RaM, SUnyaH -nyA -nyaM, gataH -tA -taM, vigataH -tA -taM. — (Out of employment) kzIRavfttiH -ttiH -tti, nirvyApAraH -rA -raM, avyApArI -riRI &c., vyApAraSUnyaH -nyA -nyaM. — (Out of office) aDikAraBrazwaH -zwA -zwaM, BrazwADikAraH -rA -raM, cyutADikAraH &c. — (To the end) avasAnaparyyantaM, antaM or SezaM yAvat, sAdyantaM; ‘hear me out,’ madva- canam avasAnaparyyantaM SfRu. — (Loudly) uccEs, uccEHsvareRa, muktakaRWaM. ‘to speak out,’ uccEHsvareRa vad. — (Openly) prakASaM, vyaktaM, prakawaM. — (In error) aparAdDaH -dDA -dDaM, BrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, sAparADaH -DA -DaM. — (Deficient) nyUnaH -nA -naM, kzIRaH -RA -RaM. — (Out of, in the sense of from) usually expressed by the abl. c. alone, or in combination with a root and some of the prep. vahis, nir, vinir, apa &c. See FROM. (Out of, in the sense of beyond) expressed by ati prefixed; as, ‘out of one's power,’ atiSakti; ‘out of the power of man,’ atimAnuzaH -zI -zaM; ‘to pass out of one's sight,’ cakzurvizayam atikram; or by the fut. pass. part.; as, ‘out of one's power,’ aSakyaH -kyA -kyaM, asADyaH -DyA -DyaM, asADanIyaH -yA -yaM; ‘out of one's reach,’ apAraRIyaH -yA -yaM, apAryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM, aprApyaH -pyA -pyaM, avizayaH -yA -yaM, vizayAtikrAntaH -ntA -ntaM; or by agocara in comp.; as, ‘out of hearing,’ ka¯rRAgocaraH -rA -raM. — (Out of, denoting exclusion, cessation, deviation from, omission, absence, dereliction, &c.) variously expressed by a, nir, vi, apa, gata, vigata, atIta, tyakta, virudDaH &c.; as, ‘out of use,’ avyavahAritaH -tA -taM; ‘out of tune,’ visvaraH -rA -raM, asvaraH &c., ‘out of fashion,’ lokavyavahAravirudDaH -dDA -dDaM; ‘out of time,’ gatakAlikaH -kA -kaMH ‘o
OUT , interj. (Out upon you, out upon it) apEhi, dUramapasara, apehi, apasara, Dik, dyE.

OUT OF: I Of place: q. v.: by abl.: to expel o. of a country: deSAnniHsArayati, B. p.: v. From.II Denoting motive: by abl., o. of fear: BayAt.: v. From.III = beyond: expr. with atItaH (tA, taM) or ati- in comp. (rare), o. of one's power: SattayatItaH (tA, taM). Ph.: gone o. of sight: cakzurvizayamatikrAntaH.IV In various senses: o. of tune: visvaraH (rA, raM); o. of use: gatavyavahAraH (rA, raM); o. of life: vigatajIvitaH (tA, taM); o. of hope: gatASaH (SA, SaM).
To OUT-ACT , v. n. aticar (c. 1. -carati -rituM); karmmaRA or kAryyeRa atikram (c. 1. -krAmati -kramituM), aDikaM kf.
OUT-DOOR , a. dvAravahiHsTaH -sTA -sTaM, dvAravahirBUtaH -tA -taM.
OUT-HOUSE , s. vAhyagfhaM, vahirgfhaM, vahiHsTagfhaM, upagfhaM.
Out-act, v. t. atyAcar 1 P, atikf 8 U.
Out-bid, v. t. aDikamUlyadAnena aBi-BU 1 P.
OUTBID: *ativadati: v. To bid.
To OUTBID , v. a. aDikamUlyaM ditsAmIti or dAtumicCAmIti vad (c. 1. vadati -dituM).
OUTBIDDER , s. aDikamUlyaditsuH m., aDikamUlyaM ditsAmIti vAdI m. (n).
To OUTBRAVE , v. a. aDikaM Barts (c. 10. Bartsayati -te -yituM), aDikaBa- rtmanena parABU.
Outbreak, Outburst, s. udBedaH, nirgamaH, prAdurBAvaH, udayaH, AsPowaH.
OUTBREAK: I Bursting forth: udBedaH.II A disturbance: saMkzoBaH.
OUTBREAK , s. udBedaH, prodBedaH, sPowaH -wanaM, savego nirgamaH.
OUTBURST , s. udBedaH, prodBedaH. See OUTBREAK, ERUPTION.

Outcast, s. nizkAsitaH, bahizkftaH, jAti-bAhyaH-BrazwaH, jAti-varRa-patitaH, apAMktaH, apAMkteyaH, patitaH. 2 caM(cAM)qAlaH, apasadaH, hInajAtiH-varRaH, vihInaH, vivarRaH, nIca-aDama-varRaH; See Mean.
OUTCAST: I An exile: nizkAsitaH (tA, taM).II = excommunicated: apapAtritaH (tA, taM). III = vagabond: KaRqitavftta (f. ttA).

OUTCAST , a. or s. (Expelled from society or one's own class or caste) jAtiBrazwaH -zwA -zwaM, jAtivahiskftaH -tA -taM, jAtivAhyaH -hya [Page560-a+ 51] -hyaM, jAtihInaH -nA -naM, hInajAtiH -tiH -ti, jAtipatitaH -tA -taM, varRaBrazwaH &c., varRahInaH &c., hInavarRaH rRA -rRaM, varRApetaH -tA -taM, paMkti- vAhyaH &c., apAMktaH -ktI -ktaM, apAMkteyaH -yA -yaM, paMktidUzakaH -kA -kaM, patitaH -tA -taM, lokavAhyaH &c., praskannaH -nnA -nnaM, vrAtyaH -tyA, juNgitaH -tA. — (Of a degraded or low caste or class) cARqAlaH -lI, caRqAlaH -lI, apasadaH, vivarRaH -rRA -rRaM, nIcaH -cA -caM, nihInaH -nA -naM, nIcajAtiH -tiH -ti, nyagjAtiH &c., antyajAtIyaH -yA -yaM, aDama- jAtIyaH &c., aDamavarRaH &c., aDamAcAraH -rA -raM, durAcAraH &c., durvfttaH -ttA -ttaM, AcArahInaH &c., AcAravarjitaH -tA -taM, pfTagjanaH, pAmaraH, jAlmaH.
Outcome, s. PalaM, pariRAmaH, udarkaH.
Outcry, s. utkroSaH, AkroSaH, kolAhalaH, kalakalaH, tumulaM, saMhUti f., udGozaH; ‘popular o(utcry)’ janaravaH-saMhUtiH. 2 Arta-nAdaH-ravaH.
OUTCRY: utkroSaH, to raise an o.: utkroSati (kruS, c. 1.), Mit.: v. Cry, noise.

OUTCRY , s. (Clamor, loud cry) kolAhalaH, utkroSaH, utkruzwaM, uccEHsvaraH, uccErGuzwaM, saMhUtiH f., bahuBiH kftA saMhUtiH, citkAraH, cItkAraH, kalakalaH, tumulaM; ‘popular outcry,’ lokApavAdaH, janApavAdaH, lokaravaH, janaravaH, janarAvaH. — (Cry of pain) ArttanAdaH.
Outdo, v. t. ati-SI 2 A, atikram 1 U, 4 P; See Excel.
OUTDO: atikrAmati (kram, c. 1.): v. To excel, surpass.
To OUTDO , v. a. atikram (c. 1. -krAmati -kramituM), aticar (c. 1. -carati -rituM), atiSI (c. 2. -Sete -SayituM), atiric in pass. (-ricyate), aBiBU. See To SURPASS.
OUTDOOR: Ph.: o. exercise: prakASavyAyAmaH (?).
OUTER: (1) bAhya (f. hyA), o. area: bAhyamaRqapaH; (2) bahis in comp., o. door: bahirdvAram.

OUTER , OUTERMOST, a. vahiHsTaH -sTA -sTaM, vAhyaH -hyA -hyaM, vahirBUtaH -tA -taM, vahirBavaH -vA -vaM, vahirvarttI -rttinI -rtti (n), vAhIkaH -kA -kaM, vahirBAgasTaH &c., vahis in comp.; as, ‘outer part,’ vahirBAgaH; ‘outer door,’ vahirdvAraM. See OUTMOST.

OUTEST , s. AramBaH, prAramBaH, praTamAramBaH, AgamaH, upakramaH, prakramaH, AdiH m., upodGAtaH; ‘at the very outset,’ praTamAramBe, AdO, AdAveva, praTamadarSanAt; ‘the outset and termination,’ Aga- manirgamO m. du., AdyantaM.
Outfit, s. sajjA, sAmagrI, upakaraRasaMBAraH, paricCedaH.
OUTFIT: sajjA: v. Equipment.
OUTFIT , s. (Equipment for a voyage, &c.) sajjA, samBAraH, sopa- kAradravyasamBAraH, samBftiH f., sAmagrI -gryaM, upakaraRasAmagrI, paricCadaH, paricCadasAmagrI, sannAhaH. — (Of a ship) nOkAsajjA.
OUTFLANK: pArSvam atikrAmati (kram, c. 1.).; etc.
OUTGENERAL: atikrAmati (kram, c. 1.) (= to surpass: q. v.).
Outgo, v. t. ati-i 2 P, aticar 1 P, atigam 1 P. [Outgo]ing, s. vyayaH, apacayaH, kzayaH, viniyogaH.
OUTGO: atyeti (i, c. 2): v. (To go) beyond, surpass.
To OUTGO , v. a. atigam (c. 1. -gacCati -gantuM), atI (c. 2. atyeti -tuM, rt. i), aticar (c. 1. -carati -rituM), atikrama (c. 1. -krAmati -kramituM).
OUTGOING , s. (Expenditure) vyayaH, apavyayaH, apacayaH, upakzayaH, viniyogaH, apahAraH; ‘incomings and outgoings,’ AyavyayO m. du.
Outgrow, v. t. atItya vfD 1 A, ati-vfD.
OUTGROW: expr. with atItya varDate (vfD, c. 1.): v. To grow, increase.
To OUTGROW , v. a. ativfG (c. 1. -varDate -rDituM), aDikaM vfD, atiSaya- vfdDiM kf, aDikavfdDiM kf, aDikavarDanaM kf.
OUTHOUSE: bahiHSAlA: v. Also shed, hut.
Outing, s. BramaRaM, paryawanaM, vihAraH.
Outlander, s. vEdeSikaH.
Outlandish, a. vijAtIya, videSIya, vi-deSaja, para-anya-deSIya. 2 asaMgata, grAmya, aSizwa, asaBya.
OUTLANDISH: vijAtIyaH (yA, yaM): v. Also un- -couth.

OUTLANDISH , a. (Foreign) videSIyaH -yA -yaM, vEdeSikaH -kI -kaM, anyade- SIyaH &c., videSajaH -jA -jaM, dUradeSIyaH -yA -yaM, paradeSIyaH &c., dUradeSavAsI -sinI -si (n), dUravAsI &c. — (Rustic, barbarous) grAmIyaH &c., grAmyaH -myA -myaM, asaByaH -ByA -ByaM, aSizwaH -zwA -zwaM, asaNgataH -tA -taM.
OUTLAST: expr. with aDikam: v. To last.
Outlaw, s. nizidDAgnyudakaH, nyAyarakzaRabAhyaH. v. t. nyAyAd bahizkf 8 U, agnyudaka-dAnaM niziD 1 P.
OUTLAW (subs.): *udGozitapAtakin (f. nI) (?); rUdDAgnyudakaH (kA, kaM) (?) (comp. agnyudakadAyinaH, Mit.); apapAtritaH (tA, taM) (?).
OUTLAW , s. vyavahAravAhyaH, nyAyarakzaRavahiHsTaH, rAjarakzaRavAhyaH, Darmmava- hiHsTaH, pAzaRqaH.

OUTLAWED , p. p. DarmmadvAravahizkftaH -tA -taM, nyAyarakzaRavahizkftaH -tA -taM, vyavahAravahirBUtaH -tA -taM, rAjarakzaRavahirBUtaH &c.

Over, prep. upari (with gen.) or in comp., aDi-UrDvaM in comp.; aDika in comp.; ‘o(ver) 20’ viMSatyaDika; gen. ex. by ati, aDi, aBi, ut, saM, with verbs; ‘cross o(ver) a river’ nadIpAraM gam 1 P. 2 (Superiority), pra, aDi, vi in comp.; ‘wander o(ver)’ pariBram 1, 4 P, paryaw 1 P; ‘o(ver) against’ aBi-saM-muKaM, aBi-prati pr. adv. parapAre, anyatIraM, pAraM-re. 2 prati, saM, ni, with verbs; ‘hand o(ver) to another’ anyasmin nikzip 6 P or saMkram c. 3 aDikaM, BUyaH, atiriktaM. 4 (Beyond) ati pr. 5 ava-, Sizwa, udvftta, aMtarita (a.); aDika in comp. 6 sAdyaMtaM, SezaM yAvat, ex. by pAra; ‘to read o(ver)’ aDi-i 2 A, pAraM gam. 7 atyaMtaM, ati-su pr., aDikaM, atiSaya-ekAMta in comp.; as a prefix of verbs, ex. by ati, atyaMtaM. 8 atIta, gata, atikrAMta, vftta, BUta; ‘o(ver) again’ punarapi; ‘o(ver) and o(ver) again’ punaH punaH, muhurmuhuH, vAraMvAraM; ‘o(ver) and above’ aparaM ca, avaSizwa a.; ‘to be o(ver)’ ex. by avasita-atIta-samApta a.; See Finish; ‘my work is o(ver)’ samAptakAryosmi; ‘in a moment all will be o(ver) with him’ kzaRena sa samAptajIvitaH-parAsuH-Bavet.

OVER (adv.): I From side to side: expr. with veDaH.II On the opposite side: apAre or parapAre.III With verbs: v. The several verbs.IV Beyond a limit: expr. with Sizwa (f. zwA): v. To remain. Ph.: (a) o. again: punarapi; (b) o. and o.: punaH punaH: v. Re- -peatedly.; (c) o. against: aBitaH (with acc.); (d) o. and above: expr. with aparaYca.

OVER (prep.): I In gen.: upari (with gen.), I found myself fallen o. a heap of dry leaves: SuzkaparRarASerUpari nipatitamAtmAnamapaSyam, K.; being o. all joy: sarvAnandAnAmupari vartamAnA, K.; God is o. the entire world: uparyupari lokaM hariH, S. k.: v. Also on, above, and the several verbs with which it is used.II More than: aDika- in comp., o. a thousand: aDikasahasra (f. srA).
OVER, BE: uparamati (ram, c. 1.): v. To cease.

OVER , prep. (Above in place, position, rank, or value) aDi, upari, UrdDva prefixed; as, ‘placed over,’ aDikftaH -tA -taM, aDi- ropitaH -tA -taM; ‘standing over,’ aDizWitaH -tA -taM, aDizWAtA m. (tf), UrdDvasTitaH &c.; ‘situated over,’ uparisTaH -sTA -sTaM; ‘heaped over,’ uparicitaH -tA -taM; ‘a tooth growing over another,’ aDidantaH. When upari is not compounded with another word it governs the gen. c.; as, ‘over all,’ upari sarvvezAM. Sometimes upari is repeated; as, uparyyupari sarvvezAM. — (From side to side, across) expressed by various prepositions, such as ati, aDi, ut, sam, aBi, vi &c.; as, ‘to cross over,’ atitF, uttF, samuttF, santF, atikram, samatikram, vyatikram, saMkram, atI; ‘to leap over,’ ullaNG, vilaNG, aBilaNG, utplu. Some- times expressed by pAraM in comp.; as, ‘to cross over a river,’ nadIpAraM gam; ‘crossing over,’ pAragaH -gA -gaM. — (Denoting superiority) expressed by pra, aDi, ut, vi, UrdDva &c. pre- fixed; as in the following words signifying pre-eminence, or ‘advantage over,’ praDAnatA, pramuKatA, aDikatvaM, ADikyaM, utkarzaH, unnatiH f., viSizwatA, UrdDvasTitiH f. — (Upon the whole surface or through the whole extent) expressed by pari, vi pre- fixed; as, ‘to wander over the earth,’ pfTivIM pariBram or paryaw or viBram. — (Over against) aBi, aBitas, prati, aBimuKaM -Kena, sammuKaM -Kena, pratimuKaM -Kena.

OVER , adv. (On the opposite side) pAre -raM; ‘the boat is over the river,’ pAragatA nOkA. — (From one to another by pass- ing) expressed by the prepositions prati, ni, sam &c., in combination with roots; as, ‘to deliver over,’ pratipad, ni- kzip, saMkram. — (Above the top, running over). See OVER- FLOWING. See To CEASE, v. n. — (To give over). See To GIVE, v. a. — (To turn over). See OVERTURN. For other senses of ‘over,’ see the verbs, &c., which follow. — (Past) vfttaH -ttA -ttaM, BUtaH -tA -taM, atItaH -tA -taM, gataH -tA -taM, atikrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, vyatItaH -tA -taM.

BU, pari- [Page562-b+ 51] pUrRIBU, jalotsekaM kf, jalotsevanaM kf, jalAplAvanaM kf, upacitaH -tA -taM BU, upacitajalaH -lA -laM BU, samAplutaH -tA -taM BU, samplutajalaH -lA -laM BU, sPAy (c. 1. sPAyate -yituM), sPItaH -tA -taM BU, sPItajalaH -lA -laM BU. — (Be exuberant) atibahulIBU, atipracurIBU, atiriktaH -ktA -ktaM BU, udriktaH &c. Overbear, v. t. vaSIkf 8 U, dam c. (damayati); ni-pat c., Dfz c. [Overbear]ing, a. Dfzwa, udData, dfpta, avalipta, garvita, utsikta; See Haughty. [Overbear]ingly, adv. sAvalepaM, sadarpaM, udDataM.

OVERWEENING: udDataH (tA, taM): v. Haughty, arrogant.
OVERWEENING , a. atyaBimAnI -ninI -ni (n), atimAnI &c., atyaha- NkArI &c., atyahaMyuH -yuH -yu, AtmaSlAGI &c.
OVERWEENINGLY: (1) sABimAnam;(2) udDatam (= Haughtily).
OVERWEENINGLY , adv. atyaBimAnena, atyahaNkAreRa, atyaBimAnapUrvvaM.
OVERWEIGHT , s. atiBAraH, aDikaBAraH, BArADikyaM, atiSayaBAraH.

Overwhelm, v. t. aBi-BU 1 P, AkulIkf 8 U, gras 1 A, Akram 1 U, 4 P; avasad c. ava-saM-mfd 9 P or c., ava-ni-pat c. nizpiz 7 P. 2 A-vf 5 U, Astf-stF 5, 9 U, AcCad 10, AkF 6 P. 3 ni-, masj c. (majjayati), gAh c., ava-vi-°, plu c., A-saM-pari-°. [Overwhelm]ed, a. aBiBUta, grasta, AkrAMta, magna, AkIrRa, upapluta, upadruta, Akula; See Overcome; ‘o(verwhelmed) with grief’ SokasamA-kula; ‘o(verwhelmed) with a flood of tears’ bAzpa-pUraparipluta.
OVERWHELM: sAdayati, ava-, (c. of sad), o. ed with grief and sorrow: duHKaSokasanna (f. nnA), Ram. ii. 59. 32.: v. Also to crush, immerge. Ph.: o. ing testimony: atiprabalaM or -pracuraM sAkzyam (?).

To OVERWHELM , v. a. (Crush, beat down) avamfd (c. 9. -mfdnAti -mardituM), pramfd, Amfd, avapat (c. 10. -pAtayati -yituM), nipat, puT (c. 10. poTayati -yituM), nizpiz (c. 7. -pinazwi -pezwuM), sampiz, vinizyiz. — (Overspread) ACad (c. 10. CAdayati -yituM), samACad, Avf (c. 5. -vfRoti -varituM -rItuM), samAvf, Akram (c. 1. krAmati -kramituM), avakF (c. 6. -kirati -karituM -rItuM), samavakF, avAkF; ‘he overwhelms them with arrows,’ tAn avAkirati SarEH. — (Immerge, sub- merge) majj (c. 10. majjayati -yituM), nimajj, avagAh (c. 10. -gAha- yati -yituM), samAplu (c. 10. -plAvayati -yituM, c. 1. -plavate), samaBiplu, aBiplu, pariplu, aBipariplu, upaplu, viplu, samAplutaM -tAM kf, pariplutaM -tAM kf, samaBiplutaM &c. kf, magnaM -gnAM kf.

OVERWHELMED , p. p. marditaH -tA -taM, avamarditaH &c., avapAtitaH &c., sampizwaH -zwA -zwaM, AcCannaH -nnA -nnaM, AcCAditaH -tA -taM, AvftaH -tA -taM, AkrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, samAkrAntaH &c., AkIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, magnaH -gnA -gnaM, nimagnaH &c., pramagnaH &c., gAhitaH &c., aBiplutaH &c., aBipariplutaH &c., samaBiplutaH &c., upaplutaH &c., pariplutaH &c., samAplutaH &c., samplutaH &c., upadrutaH &c., grastaH -stA -staM, parigataH &c., AkulaH -lA -laM; ‘with care,’ cintAmagnaH &c., cintAkulaH &c.; ‘with shame,’ hrIparigataH &c.
OVERWHELMING , part. or a. avamardI -rdinI -rdi (n), upaplavI &c., viplavakArI &c., upaplavakArakaH -kA -kaM.
OVERWISE , a. atiprAjYaH -jYA -jYaM, atijYAnI -ninI -ni (n), ekAntaprAjYaH &c., atipaRqitaH -tA -taM, paRqitammanyaH -nyA -nyaM.
Overwork, v. t. aDikaM karma kf c., atyaMtaM Ayas c. or Kid c.; (oneself) atyaMtaM pariSram 4 P, -atyAyAsaH, atikleSaH-SramaH.
OVERWORK (v.): aDikaM karma kArayati (c. of kf) (?).
OVERWORK (subs.): aDikakarman (n.) (?): v. Work.
To OVERWORK , v. a. atiSayena or ekAntataH or aDikam Ayas (c. 10. -yAsayati -yituM), atyAyAsaM or atikleSaM kf or dA.
OVERWORK , s. atyAyAsaH, atikleSaH, ekAntakleSaH, atiSramaH.
OVERWORKED , p. p. atyAyAsitaH -tA -taM, atikleSitaH &c., atiklizwaH -zwA -zwaM.
Overwrought, a. atiparizkfta.
OVERWROUGHT: perh. kArmika- in comp.: Also wrought.
OVERWROUGHT , a. atisaMskftaH -tA -taM, atiparizkftaH &c., atisidDaH -dDA -dDaM.
Overzeal, s. atyOtsukyaM, atyutkaMWA. [Overzeal]ous, a. atyutsuka, atyAsakta, ativyagra.
OVERZEALOUS: (1) atyutsukaH (kA, kaM);(2) atyutsAhin (f. nI): v. Also zealous.
OVERZEALOUS , a. atyutsukaH -kA -kaM, atyAsaktaH -ktA -ktaM, ativyagraH -grA -graM, atyuttaptaH -ptA -ptaM, aticaRqaH -RqA -RqaM, atyutkaRWitaH &c.
Oviform, a. aMqAkfti, koSAkAra.
OVIFORM , a. aRqAkAraH -rA -raM, aRqAkftiH -tiH -ti, aRqarUpaH -pA -paM.
Oviparous, a. aMqaja, dvija, dvijanman, aMqotpanna.
OVIPAROUS: aRqajaH (jA, jaM), “mUkARqajam”, Ku. iii. 42.

OVIPAROUS , a. aRqajaH -jA -jaM, aRqajanakaH -kA -kaM, aRqaprajaH -jA -jaM, aRqaprasUH -sUH -su, aRqotpAdakaH -kA -kaM, dvijaH -jA -jaM, dvijanmA -nmA -nma (n), dvijAtiH -tiH -ti, ayonijaH &c.; ‘any oviparous animal,’ dvijaH, dvijAtiH &c.

Owe, v. t. Df 10, (with dat. of creditor). 2 fRabadDa a. BU 1 P, anugfhIta a. BU; oft. ex. by pot. pass. part.; ‘you o(we) respect to your elders’ gurujanastvayA pUjyaH. [Ow]ing, a. deya, dAtavya, SoDanIya, nistArya. 2 janita, jAta, udBUta, prayukta, kA-raRa-praBava-hetu in comp.; ‘o(wing) to’ ex. by abl. or instr.; ‘to whom is your deliverance o(wing)’ kastvanmuktihetuH-kAraRaM, kena tvaM mocitaH.

OWE (v. t.): Lit.: DArayati (Df, c. 10 (with dat. of the creditor), he o. s (me) ten sovereigns: ayaM daSasuvarRakaM DArayati, Mr. ii.; God o. s liberation to the pious: BaktAya DArayati mokzaM hariH, S. k. II To be obliged for: expr. by circumlo, [Page498] I o. my darling to you: tvayEveyaM priyA me dattA, D. ii.

To OWE , v. a. (Owe money) Df (c. 10. DArayati -yituM) with acc. and dat.; as, ‘he owes a hundred pieces of money to Devadatta,’ devadattAya SataM mudrA DArayati; ‘he repaid me the money which he owed me,’ DArayan mahyaM vasUni pratyapadyata. — (Be indebted) fRI -RinI -Ri BU, fRavAn -vatI -vad BU, fRabadDaH -dDA -dDaM BU, fRaM kf. — (Be obliged) anugfhItaH -tA -taM BU; ‘I owe you many thanks for your advice,’ anugfhIto'smi tavopadeSena. The sense of ‘owe’ may be expressed by the fut. pass. [Page565-a+ 51] part.; as, ‘I owe him money,’ mayA tasmE DanaM pratideyaM or prati- dAtavyaM, or by changing the construction of the sentence thus, ‘I owe my deliverance to you,’ BavAn mama rakzAkAraRam iti jYAtavyaM. See the next word.
OWING: I Due: expr. by deyaH (yA, yaM) or prApya (f. pyA).II (On) account of: q. v.: fall of (rain) water is o. to its heaviness: apAM gurUtvAtpatanam, V. d.

OWING , part. (Due) deyaH -yA -yaM, pratideyaH -yA -yaM, dAtavyaH -vyA -vyaM, pratidAtavyaH &c., dAnIyaH -yA -yaM, SoDanIyaH -yA -yaM. — (Following as effect and cause) prayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, janitaH -tA -taM, utpAditaH &c., udBavaH -vA -vaM, praBavaH &c., kAraRaBUtaH -tA -taM; ‘my delive- rance is owing to you,’ BavAn mama rakzAkAraRaM or mama rakzaRaM BavatprayuktaM. — (Imputable) AropaRIyaH -yA -yaM, aDyAropaRIyaH -yA -yaM, sambanDanIyaH &c.
Owl, s. kOSikaH, ulUkaH, pecakaH, divA-BItaH, divAMDaH, GUkaH, niSAwanaH, vAyasArAtiH; ‘o(wl)-light’ maMdapraBA, IzatprakASaH.
OWL: (1) pecakaH;(2) u(U)lUkaH;(3) kOSikaH (rare).

OWL , s. ulUkaH, UlUkaH, pecakaH, kOSikaH, vAyasArAtiH m., divAnDaH, divABItaH, niSAwaH, niSAcaraH, naktaYcaraH, niSAdarSI m. (n), naktacArI m. (n), rajanIcaraH, kAkaBIruH m., kAvarukaH, GUkaH, vakranAsikaH, raktanAsikaH.
OWL-LIGHT , s. IzatprakASaH, mandaprakASaH, mandapraBA, niSAdiH m.

Own, a. svIya, svakIya, AtmIya, svaka, nija, AtmaBUta; sva, Atman in gen. or in comp.; ‘my o(wn)’ madIya- so tvadIya, tadIya, yuzma-dIya, asmadIya; ‘of oneʼs o(wn) accord’ svayaM, svecCayA; ‘to make oneʼs o(wn)’ AtmasAt kf 8 U. v. t. svIkf, aMgIkf, pratipad 4 A, aByupa-gam 1 P or i 2 P, grah 9 U; See Acknowledge. 2 (To be master of) ex. by svAmI, ISvaraH, patiH, aDikArI, with gen. or by (a.); or by gen. alone; ‘I o(wn) much land’ vipulaBUmeH svAmyahaM; ‘who o(wn)s this treasure’ ko'sya vittasya svAmI-patiH, kasyedaM vittaM. 3 svatvaM pratipad c. or buD c., svIya. a. iti vad 1 P; See Claim. [Own]ed, a. svIkfta; svatvaviSizwa; ‘o(wned) by me’ matsvatvaviSizwa, matsvAmika, madaDIna. [Own]er, s. svAmin m. ISvaraH, patiH, aDikArin m. ISaH, praBUH; See Lord. [Own]ership, s. svatvaM, svAmitvaM, svAmyaM, praButvaM, aDikAraH. [Own]ing, s. svIkAraH, aByupagamaH.

OWN (adj.): (1) svaH (svA, svaM), by giving my o. life: svadehArpaRena, R.; towards his o. daughter: svaduhitari, D.; your o. land: svaBUmiH, K.; (2) svakIyaH or svIyaH (yA, yaM) (= one's o.), if you want your o. life: yadi svakIyajIvanamicCasi, Vet.;(3) nijaH (jA, jaM), to his o. preceptor: nijAya gurave, Ana.;(4) svakaH (kA, kaM), went to their o. houses: svakaM svakaM niveSanaM pratyudgatAH, Kar.;(5) AtmIyaH (yA, yaM) (= one's o.), make it your o.: ayamAtmIyaH kriyatAm, K. N. B. Note that possessive pronouns are not expr. in Sanskrit.
OWN (v.): I To acknowledge: q. v.: svIkaroti.II To possess: q. v.: expr. by subs.: v. Owner, belonging to.

OWN , a. svaH svA svaM, Atma in comp., sva in comp., svakIyaH -yA -yaM, AtmIyaH -yA -yaM, svIyaH -yA -yaM, svakaH -kA -kaM, nijaH -jA -jaM, nEjaH -jI -jaM prAtisvikaH -kI -kaM, AtmasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), AtmA- DInaH -nA -naM, AtmaBUtaH -tA -taM; ‘my own,’ madIyaH -yA -yaM; ‘thy own,’ tvadIyaH -yA -yaM; ‘our own,’ asmadIyaH -yA -yaM; ‘of one's own self or own accord,’ svayaM. — (Belonging to no other) ananyasambanDI &c., ananyasvAmikaH -kA -kaM, ananyADInaH -nA -naM, ananyavarttI &c. Compounds with sva and Atma, are most frequent to express ‘own,’ as applicable to the first, second, or third person; thus, ‘one's own act,’ svakarmma n. (n), Atmakarmma, svayaNkftaM; ‘one's own son,’ svaputraH, AtmajaH, svajaH; ‘own nature,’ svaBAvaH; ‘own fancy,’ svaCandas n.; ‘own duty,’ svaDarmmaH; ‘own country,’ svadeSaH; ‘own caste or tribe,’ svajAtiH f.; ‘own family,’ svakulaM; ‘own advantage,’ svArTaH, AtmahitaM; ‘for one's own sake,’ AtmArTaM -rTe; ‘one's own wife,’ svakIyA, svIyA, svaBAryyA; ‘to make one's own,’ AtmasAtkf.

To OWN , v. a. (Have the legal right to) aDikArI -riRI -ri BU or as, svAmI &c. BU, ISvaraH -rA -rI -raM BU; ‘to own land,’ kzetrADi- kArI &c. BU, kzetrasvAmI &c. BU; or expressed by the use of as or BU with the gen. c., or with madIyaH -yA -yaM, AtmIyaH -yA -yaM, svakIyaH -yA -yaM, AtmADInaH -nA -naM, svADInaH &c.; as, ‘I own that land,’ tat kzetraM madIyam asti or AtmADInaM or mama Bavati; ‘the king owns this money,’ etad DanaM rAjADInam asti. See To BELONG. (Acknowledge to belong to one's self, claim to one's self) svIkf, AtmasAtkf, svIyamiti vad (c. 1. vadati -dituM), mameti vad, svatvam aBiman, svatvaM jYA (c. 10. jYApayati -yituM, c. 9. jAnAti) or aBijYA or buD (c. 10. boDayati -yituM), svakIyaM -yAM kf, AtmIyaM -yAM kf. — (Confess, acknowledge) svIkf, aNgIkf, urIkf, anugrah (c. 9. -gfhlAti -grahItuM), grah, aBiman (c. 4. -manyate -mantuM), aBijYA (c. 9. -jAnAti -jYAtuM), pratijYA, pratyaBijYA, samaBijYA, anuBAz (c. 1. -BAzate -zituM), svIkAraM kf.

OWNED , p. p. (Confessed, acknowledged) svIkftaH -tA -taM, aNgI- kftaH &c., aBijYAtaH -tA -taM, pratijYAtaH &c. — (The legal right vested in) svatvaviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM; ‘owned by me,’ matsvatvaviSizwaH &c.
OWNER: svAmin (f. nI), first o.: pUrvasvAmI, Vri.; sale by one who is not the o.: asvAmivikrayaH, Kat.; o. of cattle: gosvAmI, M.

OWNER , s. aDikArI m. -riRI f. (n), svAmI m. -minI f. (n), ISvaraH -rA -rI, patiH m., praBuH m., aDiBUH m., aDipaH, ISitA m. (tf), [Page565-b+ 50] netA m. (tf), nAyakaH, parivfQaH, BaraRqaH; ‘of cattle,’ gavISvaraH; ‘of land,’ kzetrADikArI m.
OWNERSHIP: (1) svatvam, creating, destroying o.: svatvajanaka (f. nikA), svatvanASaka (f. SikA), Srikrishna; partial o.: ekadeSagatasvatvam, Mit.; (2) by svAmin, to acquire o.: svAmI Bavati, Mi.
OWNERSHIP , s. svAmyaM, svAmitvaM, svatvaM, aDikAraH -ritA -tvaM, praButvaM -tA, ESvaryyaM, nAyakatvaM.
OWNING , s. (Confession) svIkAraH, svIkaraRaM, aNgIkAraH, aNgIkaraRaM.

Ox, s. vfzaBaH, vfzaH, ukzan m., balI(rI)vardaH, fzaBaH, anaquh m., gOH, BadraH, sOraBeyaH; ‘a herd of oxen’ OkzakaM; ‘a large o(x)’ mahokzaH; ‘an old o(x)’ vfdDokzaH, jaradgavaH; ‘head of a herd of oxen’ ArzaByaH; ‘an o(x) allowed to go at liberty’ zaMqaH, gopatiH, iwcaraH, ‘his shoulder’ vahaH; ‘the dewlap of an o(x)’ sAsnA, galakaMbalaH; ‘who bears the yoke’ yugyaH; DUrvoQA; ‘who draws a cart’ SAkawaH; ‘who draws a plough’ hAlikaH, sErikaH; ‘who bears a burden’ DUrvahaH, DUryaH, DurIRaH, DOreyaH, DuraMDaraH.
OX: (1) go (m.);(2) vfzaH, -BaH;(3) ukzan (m.).

OX , s. (Male of the bovine genus) gOH m. (go), vfzaBaH, vfzaH, fzaBaH, balIvarddaH, ukzA m. (n), vahataH -tiH -tuH m., kakudmAn m. (t), ana- qvAn m. (quh), SakkaraH, SAkkaraH, DAkaH, vitsanaH; ‘stupid as an ox,’ gomUQaH; ‘relating to an ox,’ OkzaH -kzI -kzaM. — (Draft ox) SaNkaH.
OX-FLY , s. gomakzikA, gomaSakaH.
OX-HIDE: (1) gavyam, Mah.;(2) ukzacarman (n.) and sim. comp.s.
OX-STALL: ukzaSAlA (?): v. Cow-pen.

OXEN , pl. gAvaH m. pl.; ‘herd of oxen,’ gokulaM, govfndaM, OkzakaM, gosamUhaH, paSugaRaH, gavyA, gotrA, pASavaM, ukzRAM saMhatiH f., garvAM vrajaH; ‘yoke of oxen,’ goyugaM, gogoyugaM; ‘property in oxen,’ goDanaM; ‘carriage drawn by oxen,’ goyAnaM.
Oxidize, v. t. ja c. Oxidation, s. jAraRaM, AtaMcanaM.
OXIDIZE: jArayati (c. of jF), Wilson: v. Also rush.
OXLIP: *ukzakandaH.
OXYD , OXIDE, s. rItiH f.; ‘of iron,’ AraM; ‘of mercury,’ rasaBasma n. (n).
To OXYDATE , OXYDIZE, v. a. jAraRaM kf, sADanaM kf, BasmIkf, AtaYcanaM kf, pratIvApaM kf; ‘oxydized iron,’ sAraRaM.
OXYDATION , s. jAraRaM, sADanaM, AtaYcanaM, pratIvApaH, BasmIkaraRaM.
OXYGEN: *prARavAyuH; sAravAyuH.
OXYGEN , s. The word used in modern treatises is amlakaraH.
OXYTONE: in gram: antodAtta (f. ttA).
OYEZ: SfRuta SfRuta (= hear), Mr.
OYEZ , OYES, SfRuta SfRuta AryyAH.
Oyster, s. Sukti f., SuktikA, muktAsPowaH; ‘o(yster)-shell’ SuktipuwaM.
OYSTER: SuktiH, -kA, o. -shell: Suktipuwam, -peSI.
OYSTER , s. SuktiH f., SuktikA, toyaSuktikA, pawolakaH, puzwikA, muktAspowaH, muktAgAraM, muktAprasUH f.; ‘oyster-shell,’ SuktipuwaM, SuktipeSI.
OYSTER-WOMAN , OYSTER-WENCH, s. SuktivikrayiRI, SuktivikretrI.
